title: Evolution‐Inspired Multi‐Objective Bayesian Optimization for Protein Engineering
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Protein engineering requires efficient navigation of vast sequence spaces under limited evaluation budgets, especially when multiple properties must be optimized simultaneously. We developed evolution‐inspired multi‐objective Bayesian optimization (EvoMOBO), an active‐learning framework that integrates path‐dependent sequence generation, global candidate competition, and explicit multi‐objective optimization, enabling efficient prioritization of high‐value variants without exhaustive library enumeration. Compared with state‐of‐the‐art methods on complete steroid receptor DNA‐binding domain (DBD) and ParD3 antitoxin landscapes, EvoMOBO achieved greater target‐region enrichment while maintaining sequence diversity across two‐ and three‐objective tasks. In the DBD landscape, optimization guided by simulation‐derived geometric descriptors enriched variants with satisfactory experimental performance without experimental labels. Building on this validation, we applied EvoMOBO to two enzyme‐engineering tasks using mechanistic descriptors, with experiments reserved for final validation. For an old yellow enzyme from Geobacillus kaustophilus , probabilities of substrate binding and reaction preorganization guided optimization of a non‐native oxidative dehydrogenation, yielding a variant that increased substrate conversion from 17.5% to 95%. For a formate oxidase from Aspergillus oryzae , stability‐related descriptors identified aggregation‐resistant variants that nearly doubled diethyl phthalate degradation in a photoenzymatic cascade. Together, these results demonstrate robust multi‐objective optimization by EvoMOBO and show that mechanism‐derived descriptors can effectively guide protein engineering toward experimentally improved functions.

title: Distinct PXR Inverse Agonism Mechanisms Rely on Differential Ligand‐induced Co‐Regulator Recruitment
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The pregnane X receptor (PXR) displays exceptional ligand promiscuity, yet the molecular basis of its antagonism remains poorly defined. PXR inhibition has traditionally been attributed to the displacement of coactivators from the activation function‐2 (AF‐2) surface. Here, we show that PXR antagonism is mechanistically heterogeneous, with distinct inhibitory mechanisms determined by ligand structure. Comparative analysis of imidazo[1,2‐a]pyridine, MI891, and SPA70 antagonists reveals multiple non‐canonical inhibitory mechanisms that decouple coregulator recruitment from transcriptional output. Notably, SPA70 preserves compatibility with coactivator recruitment while remaining transcriptionally inactive, consistent with concurrent corepressor engagement and a distinct coactivator‐compatible antagonist state. In contrast, MI891 stabilizes a PXR conformation that favors NCoR1 and SMRT binding and impairs nuclear translocation. MD simulations and mutagenesis reveal ligand‐specific perturbations of α12 and the α10/α11 region that underlie these effects. Together, these findings establish a ligand‐encoded framework for PXR antagonism that extends beyond the classical on/off switch model.

title: Each Atom and Electron Matters: A Continuous Gold Nanocluster Series
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving continuous atom‐by‐atom structural evolution and elucidating the associated quantum size effects in metal nanoclusters remain highly challenging, primarily due to the intrinsic thermodynamic preference for discrete magic‐number configurations. In this study, we present a synergistic ligand‐engineering strategy that combines dynamic ligand coordination with fluorine chemistry to break this preference. The use of weakly coordinating phosphine ligands facilitates adaptive ligand rearrangement during progressive core expansion, while fluorine‐induced noncovalent interactions establish a robust molecular and supramolecular spatial lock, thereby stabilizing cluster molecules and enhancing crystallization. Through this approach, we successfully isolated and structurally characterized an unprecedented continuous series of gold nanoclusters: Au 41 –Au 44 . Comprehensive experimental and computational structural and photophysical analyses reveal non‐monotonic geometric evolution and atom‐specific modulation of electronic structure, thereby providing direct evidence for the principle that “each atom and electron matters” in dictating cluster geometry and electronic structures. Collectively, this work fills the structural gap in medium‐sized, phosphine‐protected gold nanoclusters and provides a continuous cluster series that serves as an ideal model for probing quantum size effects at the atomic level.

title: Real‐Time Discrimination of Parallel Single‐Cell Exocytotic and Exosome Catecholamine Signaling by Multichannel Hollow Nanoelectrodes
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Chemical communication in single cells often involves multiple vesicle release pathways that can carry overlapping messenger molecules. However, existing methods cannot discriminate between these pathways simultaneously under matched conditions, making their intrinsic relationship difficult to resolve. Here we establish a multichannel hollow carbon nanoelectrode‐based strategy for real‐time discrimination of classical exocytosis and exosome‐associated release. Distinct electrochemical signatures generated within the hollow geometry enable pathway resolution, while the multichannel architecture expands effective sampling coverage over the cell surface and improves event capture efficiency. Using this approach, we show that the two catecholamine signaling routes remain active under environmental perturbation but exhibit non‐compensatory changes in release activity. Under cargo‐loading disruption, classical exocytosis retains reduced catecholamine output, whereas exosome‐associated release persists but becomes largely chemically silent. These findings uncover a previously inaccessible chemically silent state of exosome‐associated release and reveal that cells can preserve a release pathway while selectively reshaping its chemical consequence. More broadly, this work shows that parallel release routes can convey fundamentally different chemical information under the same cellular conditions and establishes a general strategy for studying pathway‐specific chemical regulation in other secretory systems.

title: CHARMM-Compatible Molecular Mechanics Force Fields for Multiscale Modeling of HIV-1 Replication Inhibitors
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into inhibitor-protein interactions and support rational drug design; however, their accuracy depends on reliable molecular mechanics force field parameters and coarse-grained representations that retain relevant molecular features. Although force field parameter sets for biomacromolecules are well established, the chemical diversity of small-molecule inhibitors often requires the development of system-specific parameters. Here, we present a parametrization framework integrating quantum mechanical optimization, experimental benchmarking, and small-molecule coarse-graining, demonstrated using HIV-1 inhibitors targeting multiple stages of the viral replication cycle. We provide a curated data set of CHARMM-compatible force field parameters for 12 HIV-1 inhibitors and the HIV assembly cofactor inositol hexakisphosphate (IP6), together with geometry-optimized atomic structures and ligand restraint files. The resulting parameters are validated against experimental structural and thermodynamic benchmarks, including lenacapavir binding free energy estimates, through inhibitor-bound complex simulations. We demonstrate applications of the parameter data set by quantifying inhibitor-protein interactions, including the free-energy profile of an integrase strand transfer inhibitor interacting with the viral capsid lattice, and the binding energetics of an allosteric integrase inhibitor. Furthermore, we extend the all-atom inhibitor parameter data set through a novel coarse-graining strategy for small molecules that preserves key electrostatic features. The HIV-1 inhibitor force field parameter data set is a publicly available resource that establishes a unified framework for multiscale modeling of HIV-1 inhibitors and facilitates computational and structural biology studies of drug resistance and inhibitor design. More generally, the framework presented here is broadly applicable to small-molecule parametrization and multiscale simulations in other therapeutic and biomolecular contexts.

title: A Homoleptic Biradicaloid‐Ligated Analogue of Ferrocene
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT In this communication, we report the synthesis, characterisation and electronic structure of a ferrocene analogue containing two biradicaloid ligands, representing the first homoleptic sandwich complex in this ligand class. In this quest, we found that the target compound was unattainable via routes involving Fe(0) or Fe(II) intermediates, and counterintuitively that the rare and much less‐explored +1 oxidation state was crucial for the synthesis.

title: A Single‐COF Photocatalytic System for One‐Pot Oxygen Reduction Coupled Ammoximation of Cyclic Ketones
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic oxygen reduction over covalent organic frameworks (COFs) has been extensively studied for H 2 O 2 production, but the in situ utilization of oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) intermediates in chemical synthesis remains underexplored. Herein, two porphyrin‐based polyimide COFs, IMCOF‐1 and IMCOF‐2, are reported as photocatalysts for the one‐pot ORR‐coupled ammoximation of cyclic ketones using O 2 and NH 4 OAc. Under light irradiation, IMCOF‐1 achieves a cyclohexanone oxime formation rate of 18.55 mmol g −1 h −1 and is effective for several other cyclic ketones. Mechanistic investigations reveal that photoinduced electron transfer from the porphyrin units to the electron‐deficient imide moieties promotes charge separation and activates O 2 at the carbonyl sites. The resulting surface‐bound *OOH intermediates are proposed to participate in ammonia oxidation and subsequent NH 2 OH formation, which then condenses with cyclic ketones to yield the corresponding oximes. In contrast to stepwise systems that first accumulate H 2 O 2 before ammoximation, the present one‐pot strategy enables the in situ utilization of oxygen‐derived reactive intermediates without requiring substantial bulk H 2 O 2 pre‐accumulation, eliminating the need for H 2 O 2 isolation, storage, and transport, thereby improving safety and atom economy while maintaining high selectivity. This work demonstrates the potential of directly harnessing ORR‐derived intermediates for the light‐driven synthesis of value‐added nitrogen‐containing chemicals.

title: Addition–Migration Cascade for Ortho ‐Selective Carbon Functionalization of Phenols
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Ortho ‐ and para ‐carbon‐disubstituted phenols are prevalent in natural products and pharmaceuticals, yet their selective synthesis remains challenging. The strong resonance‐donating effect of the hydroxyl group renders phenols electron‐rich, activates both ortho and para positions, and limits their direct functionalization with external nucleophiles. Herein, we report an addition–migration–rearomatization strategy for the ortho ‐selective carbon functionalization of phenols using readily accessible para ‐quinol carbonates and diverse organometallic nucleophiles. The transformation proceeds through nucleophilic 1,2‐addition to the dienone carbonyl, followed by C1‐to‐C2 group migration and rearomatization, thereby enabling the formal installation of carbon nucleophilic substituents at the enone α‐position. A broad range of sp 3 ‐, sp 2 ‐, and sp ‐hybridized nucleophiles, including alkyl, vinyl, aryl, heteroaryl, polyaromatic, and alkynyl reagents, participate efficiently under mild conditions. DFT calculations identify syn ‐methyl facial attack as kinetically preferred over syn ‐Boc facial attack by 24.72 kcal mol − 1 , establish that both S N 2′ manifolds are noncompetitive, and show that aromatization proceeds via a Mg‐assisted decarboxylation/deprotonation pathway rather than an unassisted route. Synthetic utility is demonstrated through a concise five step synthesis of the bioactive natural product honokiol from commercially available allyl anisole.

title: Ambipolar Electrochemical Doping of CsPbBr 3 Nanocrystals
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Electronic doping underpins many semiconductor applications but has remained elusive for lead halide perovskite nanocrystals because their high density and low formation energy of defects easily compensate introduced dopants. Here, we use electrochemical doping as a strategy to avoid doping compensation. Electrochemical injection of electrons or holes into the nanocrystal is compensated by surface-adsorbed electrolyte counterions, therefore not compromising crystal structure. We accomplished ambipolar (n- and p-type) doped CsPbBr3 nanocrystals with charge carrier concentrations ranging from intrinsic up to 4.8 × 1017 cm–3 (corresponding to 0.25 charges per nanocrystal). We show that electrochemical doping is reversible and stable at these free carrier concentrations. The extent of doping and stability are enabled by the use of lecithin, a zwitterionic ligand that strongly binds to the surface of the CsPbBr3 nanocrystals while still allowing ion and electron transfer. Lecithin stabilizes the surface atoms by shifting the potentials for Pb2+ reduction and Br– oxidation outside of the bandgap. The inferred surface-chemistry design rules for stable electrochemical doping can also serve as a guideline for developing CsPbBr3 nanocrystals stable under high free-carrier concentrations in optoelectronic devices, such as light-emitting diodes or electronically triggered quantum light sources.

title: The Elusive Fluoropolysulfates [FS 2 O 6 ] – and [FS 3 O 9 ] – , a New Class of Weakly Coordinating Anions
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT The isolation and structural characterization of the fluorodi‐ and fluorotrisulfate anions, [FS 2 O 6 ] – and [FS 3 O 9 ] – are reported. The [FS 2 O 6 ] – anion has been obtained from reactions of SO 3 with XeF 2 in the presence of PbF 2 as the salt Pb[FSO 3 ][FS 2 O 6 ] (triclinic, P , Z = 2, a = 508.65(3), b = 909.67(5), c = 969.67(5) pm, α = 89.494(2)°, β = 77.373(2)°, γ = 76.466(2)° and V = 424.99(4) Å 3 ). The [FS 3 O 9 ] – ion forms in the reaction of K[FSO 3 ] with SO 3 at room temperature as the potassium salt K[FS 3 O 9 ] (monoclinic, P 2 1 / c , Z = 4, a = 1048.69(8), b = 786.39(6), c = 969.58(7) pm, β = 90.431(2)° and V = 799.6(1) Å 3 ). The use of the [FS 3 O 9 ] – ion as a weakly coordinating anion was demonstrated with the isolation of [Se 4 ][FS 3 O 9 ] 2 (monoclinic, P 2 1 / n , Z = 2, a = 719.2(1), b = 1576.0(2), c = 897.7(1) pm, β = 113.015(5)° and V = 936.5(2) Å 3 ), obtained from the reaction of selenium, SO 3 and XeF 2 at 80°C. We investigated the anions quantum chemically concerning their molecular electrostatic potentials and the electronic energies of formation. The non–covalent interactions in [Se 4 ][FS 3 O 9 ] 2 were analysed using Quantum Theory of Atoms in Molecules (QTAIM) and Natural Bond Orbital Analysis (NBO).

title: Radical C─N Coupling at Electrified Carbon Nanotube Interfaces
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Nitrogen‐containing motifs are central to pharmaceuticals, materials, and bioactive molecules, yet controlling radical C─N bond formation under mild and catalyst‐free conditions remains challenging. Here, we report an electrified carbon nanotube (CNT) interface that promotes radical C─N coupling of aniline derivatives and N ‐containing heterocyclic compounds under ambient conditions. Mechanistic experiments show that the enhanced reactivity arises from the coupling of the applied electric field with interfacial charge transfer through the CNT network. Radical trapping, redox probing, and density functional theory calculations support a field‐assisted electron‐transfer pathway involving nitrogen‐centered radical intermediates. Our results indicate that the applied field lowers the barrier to radical generation, underscoring its critical role in enabling the reaction. This work demonstrates that conductive nanointerfaces can enable localized radical bond‐forming chemistry under an externally applied electric field.

title: Single‐Step Orientational Self‐Assembly of Pd Metallacycles and Heterometallic Pd–Pt Helical Cages From Heteroditopic Ligands
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Controlling the self‐assembly of heterometallic supramolecular architectures without generating statistical mixtures remains a major challenge. Here, we show that adaptable coordination modes of tetrazole units in heterodipotic tetrazole–pyridine ligands direct both orientational self‐sorting and selective metal organization. Reaction with cis‐protected Pd(II) acceptors afforded Pd 6 ( L ) 4 metallacycles ( L = L1 – L3 ), in which tetrazolate coordination through an unusual (2,3) binding mode is exploited in the orientational self‐sorting. In contrast, ligand L4 employed its (1,3) coordination mode together with the pyridyl donors to generate a Pd 9 ( L4 ) 6 helical cage and the heterometallic Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 , and Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cages in single‐step self‐assembly processes. Remarkably, despite the closely matched coordination preferences of Pd(II) and Pt(II), the synergistic effects of donor inequivalence and the flexible coordination behavior selectively partitions the two congeneric d 8 ions into distinct coordination sites within the Pd 3 Pt 6 ( L4 ) 6 cage. The uncommon (1,2,3) tetrazolate binding mode additionally enables formation of the Pd 9 Ag( L4 ) 6 cage. Encapsulation of enantiopure guests by the helical cages induces host chirality and corresponding chiroptical responses. These results demonstrate that coordination mode flexibility of the tetrazole moiety combined with the pyridyl unit can direct the formation of metallacycles and helical cages and enable selective partitioning of closely related metal ions in a single‐step assembly.

title: Spin‐Correlated Wavelength–Intensity Dual Modulation in Organic Diradicals via Excited‐State Channel Engineering
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Luminescent diradicals translate open‐shell spin dynamics into optical readouts, yet their spin‐dependent responses have largely been confined to emission‐intensity changes, while concurrent wavelength modulation remains rare. Here, we introduce a through‐space charge‐transfer (TSCT) strategy in which appending a δ‐carboline donor to a carbazole‐bridged diradical preserves the native through‐bond charge‐transfer (TBCT) pathway while introducing a higher‐energy TSCT‐related emissive channel. At low temperature, δCbCz(TTM) 2 exhibits pronounced magnetoluminescence (MagLum) enhancement together with an approximately 31 nm field‐induced blue shift, while zero‐field warming from 4.5 to 20 K produces an approximately 25 nm blue shift. Temperature‐dependent MagLum measurements show that the additional spectral and intensity changes induced by the magnetic field are rapidly attenuated upon warming, supporting a common spin‐dependent mechanism. The structural analogue αCbCz(TTM) 2 exhibits a similar dual response with a smaller wavelength shift, highlighting the sensitivity of the response to donor topology. Time‐resolved spectroscopy, variable‐temperature EPR, and quantum–chemical calculations support a spin‐correlated photophysical model in which magnetic and thermal perturbations regulate spin‐dependent population redistribution, thereby modulating the relative contributions of TBCT‐ and TSCT‐related emissive channels and producing correlated changes in emission intensity and wavelength. This work establishes through‐space excited‐state channel engineering as a route for extending spin‐correlated luminescence beyond intensity‐only modulation.

title: Electrostatic Cation Intercalation Into Polymeric Self‐Assembled Monolayers Enables Ambient‐Air Fabrication of 32.73% Efficient Monolithic Perovskite/Silicon Tandem Solar Cells
source: Angewandte Chemie International Edition
abstract: ABSTRACT Polymeric self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) enable stable, efficient, and scalable perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs) based on silicon heterojunction (HJT) bottom cells. However, severe steric hindrance within the polymer matrix disrupts the directional anchoring of phosphonate groups, thereby limiting macroscopic work‐function regulation and sustaining a persistent hole‐extraction barrier. Herein, we report a targeted molecular reconstruction of the buried interface via the electrostatic intercalation of phenethylammonium iodide (PEAI). Templated by the polymer backbone, the intercalated PEA + cations adopt a highly directional vertical arrangement. This oriented molecular scaffold provides a strong intrinsic dipole while driving the electronegative iodide (I − ) counterions to enrich at the uppermost interface. This synergistic spatial decoupling maximizes the net upward dipole, triggering a favorable energy level realignment that effectively overcomes the hole extraction barrier. Concurrently, the halide‐enriched SAM dictates crystallization kinetics during ambient‐air slot‐die coating, inducing rapid “burst nucleation” to minimize solvate intermediates and suppress basal voids. Consequently, our 1 cm 2 TSC achieves an independently certified power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 32.73%. Benefiting from monolithic crystallographic integrity, the unencapsulated device maintains an enhanced T 80 lifetime of 2182 h under continuous maximum power point tracking.

title: High‐Density Pixelated Metasurfaces for Terahertz Hyperspectral Imaging
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Metasurface‐enabled terahertz imaging and spectroscopy are moving toward compact, high‐throughput systems, but current approaches remain limited by discrete spectral sampling, computational reconstruction, and the trade‐off between spatial resolution and resonance quality in nonlocal designs. Here, we introduce a fundamentally different paradigm based on photonic crystal heterojunction‐enabled pixelated metasurfaces that directly encode spatial information into spectrally resolved, high‐quality‐factor resonances. By embedding bound‐state‐in‐the‐continuum metapixels within a bandgap‐engineered heterostructure, we simultaneously suppress lateral leakage and control vertical radiation, enabling effective three‐dimensional photon confinement in finite metasurfaces. This mechanism overcomes the conventional dependence of resonance quality on pixel size, yielding enhanced quality factors and figure of merit without increasing the device footprint, and enabling metapixels with lateral dimensions of ∼2λ that retain high spectral fidelity and signal‐to‐noise ratio. Leveraging this capability, we realize a 3 × 3 pixelated metasurface supporting nine independently addressable resonances, all retrieved in a single‐shot broadband terahertz measurement. The resulting spectral‐spatial encoding strategy establishes a direct one‐to‐one mapping between resonance signatures and spatial pixels, enabling hyperspectral imaging with a single‐pixel detector and a THz pulse, without raster scanning or algorithmic inversion. These results provide a scalable route toward real‐time terahertz imaging and integrated photonic sensing.

title: Sustainable Soft Electronic Devices by High‐Performance Recyclable Elastomers and Conductors
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Soft electronics have driven emerging advancements, which are expected to have wide‐range and large‐scale applications in health management, electronic skins, soft robotics, and interactive human‐machine interfaces. However, existing strategies mainly focus on isolated components, and system‐level soft electronic devices combining sustainable fabrication, robust performance, and versatile integrated functions have rarely been explored. Herein, we develop a recyclable soft electronic system enabled with multifunctional poly thioctic acid (TA) elastomer and high‐performance elastic metallic conductors. The multifunctional TA elastomer exhibits an exceptional combination of stretchability (435% strain), fracture energy (5.5 kJ/m 2 ), apparent adhesion energy on Cu (10.7 kJ/m 2 ), and thermal conductivity (0.69 W/m·K). These properties enable robust mechanical and electronic interfacing with different electronic components for sustainable soft circuits, while also endowing the electronic systems with outstanding self‐healing and recycling capabilities. Furthermore, by integrating with printable and recyclable elastic conductors based on eutectic liquid metals, the sustainable soft electronic systems can fully restore circuit functionality after complete mechanical rupture with the selfhealing capability of the composite elastomer and the elastic conductor. The system can be reprocessed to achieve full functionality restoration. The materials strategy developed in this study renders a promising solution for the development of soft and sustainable electronic devices.

title: Designing a Thermochemically Active Hydrogel With In Situ‐Formed Ceramic–Carbon Hybrid Barrier for Suppressing Thermal Runaway Propagation
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Preventing thermal runaway propagation (TRP) is critical for the safety of lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). While hydrogel interlayers actively cool through water evaporation, their mechanical reinforcement with conventional fillers dilutes the water‐rich matrix and reduces enthalpy. Here, we propose a paradigm‐shifting strategy by using boric acid (BA) as a thermochemically active cross‐linker in a poly(AMPS) hydrogel. BA reconstructs the hydrogel network through dual N─H⋯O hydrogen bonding and B⋯O═C coordination, simultaneously enhancing compressive strength by 567%. Upon thermal runaway, the composite provides dual‐mode protection: (1) synergistic heat absorption (volumetric enthalpy > 2000 J cm − 3 ) via water evaporation and BA stepwise dehydration, accompanied by flame‐inhibiting SO 2 release. (2) In situ formation of a highly insulating ceramic–carbon hybrid barrier. Post‐test analysis reveals a critical BA content of 25 wt%, where tetrahedral boron coordination (63.3% BO 4 ) maximizes covalent B─O─C bonds that chemically “weld” B 2 O 3 to carbon. This trend in BO 4 fraction with BA loading quantitatively explains the exceptional TRP suppression, reducing the adjacent cell's peak temperature by over 500°C. Beyond a high‐performance material, this work establishes a general design principle: employing reactive fillers that orchestrate both multi‐stage energy management and tailored barrier synthesis, paving the way for next‐generation battery safety materials.

title: Ion–Electron Coupling Transport in Semiconductor Nanotubes for Retinomorphic Vision
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT A key limitation of current artificial visual systems lies in their single‐channel signal transduction, which fundamentally departs from the parallel processing architecture of the biological retinas enabled by rod and cone cells. To bridge this gap, we developed a retinomorphic vision device by ion‐electron coupling transport based on carbon nanotube (CNT)/zinc oxide (ZnO) heterostructured nanotubes. Upon optical stimuli, this device generates two distinct ionic and electronic current signals, effectively mimicking the parallel phototransduction pathways in biological vision. This dual‐channel property enables efficient machine vision perception, achieving luminance adaptation and color discrimination accuracies of 96.5% and 98.2%, respectively. Furthermore, traffic‐light‐guided closed‐loop navigation of a mobile vehicle in a real scene has verified its application potential in embodied intelligence. This “single device enabled, distinguishable dual‐channel readouts” principle opens a new avenue toward artificial vision systems.

title: Ultralow Loading Iridium Doped Hollandite Manganese Oxide Nanowires for Efficient Acidic Oxygen Evolution Reaction
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient and durable catalysts for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) are critical for hydrogen production but remain limited by reliance on scarce iridium (Ir). We present an ultralow‐loading Ir catalyst (3 at%, − 2 ) integrated within a hollandite MnO 2 framework, which lowers the overpotential at 10 mA cm − 2 from 580 mV (undoped α‐MnO 2 ) to 303 mV and delivers an Ir mass activity an order of magnitude higher than commercial IrO x . Varying pH and potential, we combine ICP‐MS dissolution measurements with x‐ray absorption spectroscopy, electron energy loss spectroscopy, and 4D scanning transmission electron microscopy. Dissolution is modest, with at least 79% of the Ir and 76% of the Mn remaining after 6 h under applied potential, and Ir remains oxidized and associated with the hollandite framework. Mn, in contrast, undergoes pH‐ and potential‐dependent reduction and local structural disorder. Notably, the strongest Mn reconstruction (pH 0, 1.65 V) coincides with moderate dissolution, whereas the greatest Ir and Mn loss (pH 0, 1.60 V) occurs where the residual material is less reconstructed. Net dissolution therefore does not report on local structural change, highlighting the need to evaluate dissolution, reconstruction, and oxidation state together when designing and assessing Ir‐efficient mixed‐metal oxide catalysts.

title: A Dual‐Locked and H 2 S‐NO Tandem‐Activatable NIR‐II Nanoagent for Colon Cancer Theranostics
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Dual‐locked activatable theranostics have been emerging as a promising cancer therapy platform. However, most of the reported dual‐locked systems only restricted to enzyme‐responsive probes, new molecular tools with other biomarker‐responsiveness still remain challenging. Moreover, optical manipulation in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window can potentially boost the theranostic efficacy, but having rarely been explored. In this study, we report a dual‐locked and gas tandem‐activatable NIR‐II nanoagent for colon cancer theranostics. Water‐dispersible nanoparticles containing a nitrated organic small molecule (CTBN) and an acid‐responsive NO donor (NONOate; CTBNN‐NPs) are fabricated, displaying negligible emission in visible‐NIR region. Upon uptake by colon cancer cells, CTBNN‐NPs can be tandemly activated by the overexpressed H 2 S and the in situ released NO, thus turning on NIR‐II emission extending to 1200 nm. Moreover, the activated CTBNN‐NPs also demonstrate augmented NIR absorption as well as robust photothermal and type‐I photodynamic performance, achieving NIR‐II fluorescence imaging‐guided efficient photo‐elimination of colon cancer together with NO gas therapy, while exhibiting limited efficacy in the tested cervical and breast cancer models. This work provides a new molecular design approach to dual‐locked and H 2 S‐NO tandem‐activatable nanoagents with gas‐responsive and NIR‐II active capabilities, highlighting the exciting potential for cancer theranostics.

title: Defined Matrices Reveal Epithelial‐ and Mesenchymal‐Specific Responses to Stiffness and Adhesion in Human iPSC‐Derived Intestinal Organoids
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Human intestinal organoids (hIOs) are powerful models for studying development and disease, yet dissecting how physical and matrix cues shape epithelial and mesenchymal responses remains challenging due to reliance on ill‐defined matrices. Here, a fully defined hIO workflow was developed in which Matrigel was replaced by recombinant human substrates during pluripotent stem cell differentiation and by polyethylene glycol (PEG) hydrogels during 3D culture, while maintaining organoid viability and epithelial cytodifferentiation. Transcriptomic analyses show that both PEG‐ and Matrigel‐cultured hIO epithelial cells are most similar to human duodenal reference populations, and have greater transcriptional similarity to fetal than adult duodenal references. Despite this overall similarity, PEG culture is associated with subtle shifts in epithelial differentiation‐associated gene expression, together with altered mesenchymal ECM‐remodelling and integrin‐associated programs. Increasing matrix stiffness produces modest effects in epithelial cells, including increased MUC2‐positive cells, whereas mesenchymal transcriptional responses to stiffness are limited. Together, these findings establish a fully defined hIO platform that retains responsiveness to inflammatory stimulation while enabling controlled investigation of how matrix composition and stiffness shape epithelial and mesenchymal cell states in models of intestinal development and fibrosis.

title: Pd Single‐Atom Engineered Janus BiOCl/MXene Heterostructure for Printed Self‐Decoupled Temperature‐Humidity Dual‐Mode Sensors
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The advancement of flexible sensing technologies is of paramount importance in biomedical engineering. However, achieving high‐fidelity multi‐modal temperature‐humidity sensing without inter‐channel cross‐talk and computational post‐processing remains a formidable challenge due to overlapping transduction mechanisms. In this study, an unprecedented electron‐ion synergistic functional material, featuring a unique inherent self‐decoupling capability, was developed based on the Janus hierarchical heterostructure. Through interfacial chemical engineering of Pd single‐atom anchoring and heterogeneous‐nucleation‐driven vertical growth of BiOCl on hollow MXene, the constructed material architecture successfully establishes fundamentally segregated electronic and ionic stimulus‐response pathways. Specifically, humidity fluctuations trigger ultra‐fast quasi‐2D proton conduction facilitated by localized potential wells and electronic redistribution generated around atomically dispersed Pd sites, while temperature gradients induce entropy‐driven carrier diffusion within the conductive MXene network. By suppressing signal cross‐talk through rigorous mechanistic orthogonality, the fabricated sensing array exhibits outstanding response characteristics (37.5/50 ms for humidity response/recovery and 25/62.5 ms for high/low‐temperature response), alongside superior oxidation resistance and robust functional durability (enduring 5000 cycles of testing). Ultimately, leveraging this multi‐modal sensing platform and machine learning algorithm, the integrated closed‐loop therapeutic system enables accurate evaluation of wound healing progression as well as on‐demand drug release, pioneering a new paradigm for next‐generation flexible electronics and adaptive healthcare modalities.

title: Preserving Polymorphic Crystalline Structures in Bulk Heterojunctions for Efficient Organic Solar Cells
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT The crystal structure of a material profoundly influences its physical, optical, and electronic properties. However, precise control over polymorph formation of non‐fullerene acceptors (NFAs) in bulk heterojunction active layers remains challenging for optimizing organic solar cell (OSC) performance. Here, we employ a non‐halogenated mixed‐solvent system comprising carbon disulfide (CS 2 ) and o‐xylene (OXY) to selectively regulate the crystallization of the high‐performance acceptor BTP‐eC9. A specific polymorph (Form II) is preferentially induced and consistently identified in powder, neat‐film, and bulk heterojunction samples by correlating wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (WAXS) and grazing‐incidence wide‐angle x‐ray scattering (GIWAXS) patterns with simulations derived from the corresponding single‐crystal structures. Compared with Form I, Form II exhibits improved optoelectronic properties, including extended exciton diffusion length, balanced charge mobility, and suppressed non‐radiative recombination. Consequently, Form II‐based devices achieve a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 20.61% with a fill factor of 82.85%, representing a 27.0% relative improvement over Form I devices (PCE = 16.23%). Moreover, this method enables scalable manufacturing, with flexible OSCs (1 cm 2 active area) fabricated by slot‐die coating achieving a PCE of 17.93%. This work establishes a practical pathway for solution‐processed polymorph control and reveals the relationship among single‐crystal packing, acceptor molecular packing, and device performance.

title: Upcycling Piezoelectric Single‐Crystal Debris Into High‐Performance Flexible 0–3 Composites
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐value piezoelectric single‐crystal debris remains an untapped resource for flexible electromechanical materials. Although relaxor‐based ferroelectric single crystals offer exceptional piezoelectric properties, off‐cuts inevitably generated during precision processing are typically discarded because their irregular geometries prevent direct device integration. Here, we report a recycling‐to‐device upcycling strategy that converts industrial Pb(Mg 1/3 Nb 2/3 )O 3 –PbTiO 3 (PMN–PT) single‐crystal debris into high‐performance flexible 0–3 piezoelectric composites and energy harvesters through material–structure–mechanics co‐design. A ball‐milling‐based particle refinement procedure converts the debris into dispersible particulate fillers, while dielectrophoresis (DEP)‐assisted curing reorganizes randomly dispersed particles in a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) matrix into vertically connected quasi‐1–3‐like networks. The polymer matrix provides mechanical tunability, allowing flexibility and dynamic stress transfer to the aligned single‐crystal network to be jointly optimized. The optimized composite achieves a d 33 of 118.5 pC N −1 while retaining mechanical flexibility, placing it among the highest‐performing flexible 0–3 piezoelectric composites. Comparative experiments and finite‐element simulations reveal that single‐crystal‐derived fillers exhibit stronger DEP‐induced enhancement than polycrystalline counterparts owing to more coherent intraparticle electromechanical conversion. Integrated into flexible energy harvesters, the optimized composite delivers a peak areal power density of 284.2 µW cm − 2 . This work establishes a scalable upcycling pathway for reutilizing high‐value functional crystal waste in flexible self‐powered electromechanical systems.

title: Fluoride‐Mediated Host‐Activator Engineering in Homogeneous Lithium Glass Scintillators for Thermal‐Neutron Detection and Imaging
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Homogeneous lithium‐aluminosilicate‐glass scintillators offer transparency, scalable fabrication, and compositional flexibility, but their neutron response is limited by defect trapping and activator loading concentration. Here, fluoride‐mediated host‐activator engineering is introduced to overcome these coupled limitations in Ce 3+ ‐activated lithium aluminosilicate glasses. F − preferentially coordinates with Li + and Mg 2+ , preserving the primary Si/Al─O tetrahedral units while reorganizing inter‐tetrahedral linkages. The resulting host‐network reconfiguration suppresses electronic disorder and defect‐mediated trapping, modulates medium‐range Ce‐centered correlations, broadens the viable Ce‐concentration window, and enables efficient excitation capture at ∼9 wt% CeO 2 (twice that of GS20). After 6 Li enrichment, it delivers 8003 photons neutron −1 , an energy resolution of 6.8%, a decay time of 85.06 ns, and a neutron peak‐to‐trough ratio of 77:1. To the best of our knowledge, these values represent the highest light yield and best energy resolution reported for a homogeneous transparent 6 Li‐enriched glass scintillator, achieving single‐digit neutron energy resolution for the first time and approaching the performance of 3 He proportional counters and high‐performance crystalline scintillators. A transparent plate exceeding 2 inches further enables proof‐of‐concept two‐dimensional thermal‐neutron imaging with a system‐level spatial resolution of 1.35 mm, demonstrating the scalability of the glass for position‐sensitive neutron imaging.

title: Daily briefing: The ‘overshoot COP’ kicks off
source: Nature
abstract: The COP31 climate conference begins, with ‘climate overshoot’ a key talking point. Plus, the surprising benefits of ‘pink noise’ and the role of AI chatbots to support men’s mental health.

title: pH‐Responsive Synthetic Cells for Programmable In Situ Protein Synthesis and Release
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Lipid membrane‐bound synthetic cells provide programmable, cell‐like compartments for on‐demand biomolecule production. However, most cell‐free gene expression systems in synthetic cells are regulated by user‐imposed cues rather than signals associated with environmental or physiological states. Here, we present an acidity‐transducing synthetic cell that converts external pH changes into nucleic acid information to drive in situ protein synthesis. The system integrates gramicidin A proton channels for pH sensing, triplex‐forming single‐stranded DNA (ssDNA) that releases a trigger ssDNA upon acidification, and a toehold switch RNA that activates translation in response to the released trigger ssDNA. This work further reveals that tuning the annealing length between the pH‐responsive and trigger ssDNAs controls the trigger‐release pH, which is critical for enabling acid‐triggered protein synthesis. The synthetic cells retain their pH‐responsive activity when embedded in alginate hydrogels, creating acidity‐responsive materials that synthesize proteins in situ rather than release preloaded cargo. Cell‐penetrating peptide tagging further enables selective protein release and target‐specific binding. This work establishes a molecular transduction strategy for programming synthetic cell materials to sense environmentally relevant acidity and generates functional biomolecules on demand.

title: Skunk Cabbage‐Inspired AIEgen Photoactuators With Multiwavelength Response, Ultrafast Actuation, and Multicolor Fluorescence
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Near‐infrared (NIR)‐responsive polymer actuators doped with inorganic photothermal agents face trade‐offs between photothermal performance and mechanical properties due to limited compatibility. Besides, most systems remain confined to 808 nm operation, as extending to 980 nm is hindered by poor absorption. Inspired by skunk cabbage thermogenesis, we develop ultra‐fast, multicolor fluorescent NIR‐responsive actuators by integrating aggregation‐induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) with excellent compatibility and photothermal properties into Janus‐structured polyimides (PIs) at ultra‐low doping (0.25 wt%). The multi‐donor‐π structure of AIEgen achieves redshifted NIR absorption extending to 980 nm and enhanced photothermal abilities through boosted intramolecular donor–acceptor interactions and molecular motion‐facilitated nonradiative decay (MMFND). Mirroring the mitochondrial working mode, AIEgens are uniformly embedded within PIs without compromising structural integrity, preserving mechanical properties above 100 MPa. Under NIR illumination, PI actuators achieve deformation with a bending speed of 900°/s, which facilitates crawling, gripping, and rapid continuous bidirectional flipping. The combination of multiwavelength photoresponse and multicolor fluorescence endows materials with dynamic information encoding. Programmable motions are implemented under different wavelengths through sequential, penetrative, and heat‐transfer actuation. This work provides guidelines for smart materials requiring precise 980 nm actuation with maintained mechanical robustness.

title: Dynamic, Wet‐Adhesive Hydrogels for Enhanced Interface Healing in Cartilage Repair
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Articular cartilage defects remain a major clinical challenge due to the tissue's limited self‐repair capacity. Although numerous biomaterial‐based strategies have been explored, achieving a stable and functional cartilage interface remains difficult. A critical barrier is the poor integration between grafts and native cartilage, leading to fibrocartilage formation, delamination, and repair failure. Current approaches show limited success due to inadequate wet adhesion, mechanical mismatch, and insufficient chemical bonding. Here, we report a dynamically adaptive wet‐adhesive hydrogel composed of oxidized hyaluronic acid, quaternized chitosan, and silk fibroin (OHA/QCS/SF) for enhanced cartilage interface healing. The precursor exhibited rapid underwater spreading on hydrated substrates and displaced interfacial fluid in a fluid‐covered assay. Fluorescence imaging further revealed wetting and infiltration into the PAAm hydrogel. Dynamic Schiff‐base bonding between aldehyde groups in the hydrogel and amine‐containing components at the cartilage interface further promoted wet adhesion, while the reversible network enabled self‐healing under mechanical disturbance. In a rabbit cartilage defect model, the hydrogel loaded with synovial membrane‐derived mesenchymal stem cells (SMSCs) improved defect filling, host–graft integration, and cartilage‐like regeneration. This study provides a dynamic wet‐adhesive hydrogel strategy for improving biomaterial–cartilage interface healing in fluid‐rich joint environments.

title: Liquid Luminescent Materials Based on 10 H ‐Pyrido[1,2‐ a ]‐5‐indolium Salts
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Next‐generation flexible optoelectronics and soft robotics require adaptive luminescent materials that withstand extreme environments while remaining deformable. However, the photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of current solvent‐free ionic liquids suffers from fundamental limitations arising from aggregation‐caused quenching and rapid nonradiative decay, and these liquids degrade under thermal and chemical stress. This study presents a supramolecular locking strategy that overcomes these limitations through kinetically stabilized anion–π + interactions. Specifically, a rigid N‐doped fluorene (10 H ‐pyrido[1,2‐ a ]‐5‐indolium, PIn + ) was paired with selected anions to maintain fluidity and suppress nonradiative molecular motion by locking radiative pathways in the liquid state. This ionic tethering approach yielded an unprecedented PLQY of 80% in the liquid state while preserving the solvent‐free liquid nature of the material. These highly emissive ionic liquids exhibited extreme physicochemical robustness, withstanding thermal decomposition up to 400°C, retaining intense emission without volatilization even under reduced pressure at 250°C, and resisting strongly acidic and basic environments. Derived from a versatile and readily synthesizable fluorene platform, this system also provides broad opportunities for structural customization. These findings establish a general molecular design principle for highly robust and emissive liquid fluorophores, providing a foundation for indestructible and flexible photonic technologies operating under extreme conditions.

title: Understanding Charge Acceptance Limitations During Extreme Fast‐Charging of Li‐ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Extreme fast charging in lithium‐ion batteries is limited by their poor charge acceptance at high C‐rates. We use overpotential component analysis to decouple ohmic, kinetic and transport voltage losses during fast charging. The concentration gradients are identified as the primary culprit in poor charge acceptance, so we study carbonate electrolytes that utilize acetonitrile, a low viscosity, high dielectric liquid, as a co‐solvent to improve ion transport. Our results indicate acetonitrile co‐solvent successfully reduces fast charging concentration gradients and therefore improves charge acceptance at high C‐rates, particularly when used in combination with interface‐stabilizing additives. Molecular dynamics simulations show that ACN enhances Li + transport through a combination of reduced bulk viscosity and increased solvation‐shell lability, with shorter solvent residence times and faster coordination exchange producing transport gains beyond those expected from viscosity reduction alone. Finally, we use three‐electrode cells to deconvolute overpotential at each electrode, and the specific LiNi 0.8 Mn 0.1 Co 0.1 O 2 (NMC811) electrode architecture and loading used in our study is found to have much higher overpotentials than our graphite electrode. In particular, the significant differences in NMC811 concentration gradients between electrolytes with or without acetonitrile indicate that the design of electrode architecture is crucial for extreme fast charging applications.

title: Data‐Driven Host Microstructure Design Toward Efficient and Durable Room‐Temperature Sodium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Porous carbon materials are critical hosts for chalcogen‐ and halogen‐based conversion‐type cathodes, as they govern the activity and durability of electrochemical reactions. Understanding how their microstructures regulate electrolyte‐electrode interactions remains challenging given multiple coupling factors and dynamic changes during electrochemical cycling. Herein, machine learning was first used to screen three pore structure parameter windows relevant to electrochemical features from a large experimental dataset (23 carbon hosts and 1055 specific‐capacity data points). Based on these screened windows, three representative carbon hosts, namely micropore‐rich carbon, balanced carbon, and meso/macropore‐rich carbon, were synthesized as model systems. We reveal that pore structure governs sulfur species evolution, thereby dictating the competition between polysulfide‐mediated reactions and solvent self‐decomposition. The resulting spatial‐compositional differences of the cathode–electrolyte interphase (CEI) were found to profoundly impact energy efficiency, reversibility, and rate performance. The balanced carbon cathode with optimized inorganic‐organic distribution delivers an initial capacity of 1249.4 mAh g −1 and retains a capacity of 784.8 mAh g −1 after 500 cycles. This work not only proposes a data‐driven strategy for identifying CEI‐relevant pore structure windows, but also provides mechanistic insight into how physical metrics of porous carbon modulate multi‐step complex reactions and ultimately influence electrochemical performance.

title: cis – trans Isomerism Enables Visible Light‐Excited Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence and Dynamic Afterglow
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Isomerism serves as a powerful strategy for modulating organic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP), which is crucial for developing novel RTP materials and elucidating structure‐property relationships. However, cis – trans isomerism that is widespread in organic compounds has not been deeply explored in terms of its influence on RTP properties. In this study, the cis – trans isomers of two 9,10‐dihydrophenanthrene‐9,10‐dicarbonitriles, DPCN‐H and DPCN‐O (with OMe group), are designed and synthesized. Significant differences in luminous behavior are observed between the cis‐ and trans ‐isomers. The trans ‐DPCNs exhibit notably superior RTP and afterglow performance compared to cis ‐DPCNs for their better structural planarity and tighter packing. Among them, trans ‐DPCN‐O achieves an afterglow quantum yield as high as 43% upon visible‐light excitation. Additionally, trans ‐DPCN‐H displays excitation‐power‐dependent and temperature‐dependent afterglow color modulation, while the nanoparticles of trans ‐DPCN‐O demonstrates efficient visible‐light‐excited afterglow in aqueous solution. The excellent RTP properties of the trans‐ DPCNs enable their successful application in complex anti‐counterfeiting with four dimensions, and in vivo imaging in mice under white LED excitation with a signal‐to‐noise ratio of up to 228. This work presents the first investigation into how cis – trans isomerism affects organic RTP and provides new insights into designing high‐performance RTP materials.

title: A Closed‐Loop‐Recyclable Liquid‐Crystalline Dynamic Covalent Network Soft Actuator Derived From Nonliquid‐Crystalline Monomers
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid‐crystalline networks constructed from nonliquid‐crystalline precursors offer an alternative to conventional routes based on liquid‐crystalline monomers, that is, mesogenic monomers. Here, we report a closed‐loop recyclable liquid crystal polymer network (CLLCP) synthesized from nonliquid‐crystalline aldehyde and amine building blocks through reversible imine chemistry. Imine formation constructs mesogenic segments and establishes network connectivity, linking liquid‐crystalline structural design with chemical recyclability. This approach avoids pre‐synthesis of liquid‐crystalline monomers and offers flexibility in the selection of network components. The combination of rigid imine‐linked segments and flexible spacers supports liquid‐crystalline order and segmental mobility, while dynamic imine bonds enable stress relaxation and thermal reprocessing. Aligned CLLCP films exhibit a reversible thermomechanical actuation strain of 26% with good cycling stability. Under acidic conditions, imine hydrolysis disassembles the network and enables recovery of the four original molecular building blocks. These components are reused to reconstruct networks with phase behavior, mechanical properties, and actuation performance comparable to those of the pristine materials. This molecular design couples in situ mesogenic‐segment construction with polymer‐to‐monomer closed‐loop recycling, providing a modular route to sustainable liquid‐crystalline soft actuators.

title: Coordination Number‐Tuned FeN x Single‐Atom Nanozymes for Sustained Peroxidase‐Like Catalysis in Tumor Therapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Peroxidase (POD)‐like catalysis by single‐atom nanozymes (SAEs) under sustained H 2 O 2 exposure requires both rapid substrate activation and durable catalytic turnover, both of which are closely linked to the coordination environment of metal sites. However, how the coordination number governs their balance remains unclear, especially when the interaction strength between SAEs and H 2 O 2 is tuned. Herein, we construct three structurally comparable FeN x ‐SAEs (x = 4, 3, and 2), revealing a volcano‐like relationship between POD‐like activity and H 2 O 2 adsorption strength. The selected FeN 3 ‐SAE exhibits the highest POD‐like activity (1.52 × 10 −6 M s −1 ), which is 1.9‐ and 4.1‐fold greater than those of FeN 2 ‐SAE and FeN 4 ‐SAE, respectively. Moreover, the FeN 3 ‐SAE sustains efficient H 2 O 2 consumption and robust •OH generation during prolonged catalysis, whereas the FeN 4 ‐SAE suffers from inadequate H 2 O 2 activation, and the FeN 2 ‐SAE undergoes rapid kinetic decay. Combined experiments and theoretical calculations attribute this performance to well‐balanced H 2 O 2 adsorption at the FeN 3 site, which facilitates substrate activation, intermediate desorption, and active‐site regeneration. Both cellular and animal experiments reveal that FeN 3 ‐SAE enables continuous H 2 O 2 conversion into cytotoxic •OH, depleting GSH and triggering tumor suppression accompanied by immune activation. This study provides mechanistic insights into sustained POD‐like catalysis from the perspective of coordination number‐regulated adsorption‒turnover balance.

title: Deep-Learning-Empowered Gold Nanoparticle Dimer-Assisted Hyperbolic Metamaterial Surface Plasmon Resonance Fiber-Optic Sensor for Ultrasensitive Mercury Ion Detection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Mercury ions (Hg2+) are highly toxic heavy-metal contaminants that pose serious environmental and health hazards, necessitating the development of highly sensitive and accurate detection methods. Herein, a fiber-optic surface plasmon resonance (SPR) sensor is developed for the ultrasensitive detection of Hg2+. The sensing probe is constructed on a hyperbolic metamaterial (HMM) consisting of three repeated Ag/ITO bilayers, decorated with thymine (T)-rich DNA-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). Upon Hg2+ addition, specific T–Hg2+–T coordination captures a second population of DNA-functionalized AuNPs, forming AuNP dimers on the HMM surface. The nanometer interparticle gap of the AuNP dimer induces strong plasmonic coupling, which amplifies the local refractive index (RI) changes at the sensing interface and produces a pronounced SPR wavelength shift, enabling highly sensitive detection of Hg2+. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed sensor exhibits a peak RI sensitivity of 8600 nm/RIU and achieves a limit of detection as low as 2.63 pM for Hg2+. Moreover, a DenseNet-based deep-learning model is employed to extract subtle spectral features from SPR spectra acquired at seven Hg2+ concentration levels, enabling quantitative concentration prediction with an R2 of 0.998505. Therefore, the proposed fiber-optic SPR sensor provides a promising strategy for sensitive and accurate Hg2+ detection.

title: Sensitive, Broadband, and Stable Short‐Wave Infrared Photodetection and Imaging in Mixed‐Dimensional Organic/Inorganic Heterostructures
source: Advanced Materials
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional short‐wave infrared (SWIR) photodetectors confront cost disadvantages and fabrication complexity, whereas two‐dimensional (2D) van der Waals devices exhibit inherent performance limitations. Mixed‐dimensional organic/inorganic heterostructures offer a promising strategy for SWIR photodetection, synergizing strong optical absorption and tunability of organic semiconductors with high charge mobility and stability of inorganics. However, critical challenges remain in architecture design, including optimal carrier‐collection geometry, material selection, and interface engineering for boosting devices’ performance. Herein, a type‐II band‐aligned PTF/WSe 2 mixed‐dimensional heterostructure is reported for high‐performance broadband SWIR photodetection via heterostructure synergy and rational Schottky barrier engineering. The Cr/ p ‐WSe 2 /PTF configuration (∼ 0.28 eV barrier) achieves superior performance, while Cr/ n ‐WSe 2 /PTF suffers from a higher barrier (∼ 1.18 eV). The optimized device achieves broad spectral photoresponsivity (∼ 10 3 A/W, 1060–1470 nm) and exceptional performance at 1310 nm: ultrahigh photoresponsivity ( R = 2894 A/W), robust specific detectivity ( D * = 1.0×10 12 Jones), and excellent long‐term ambient stability. Versus standalone PTF, it delivers 17‐fold higher photoresponsivity and 96% lower bias voltage. High‐resolution SWIR image‐pattern reconstruction, together with concurrent performance improvements after six months of controlled storage, validates this PTF/WSe 2 mixed‐dimensional heterostructure's potential for advancing next‐generation high‐performance SWIR detectors.

title: Bismuth‐Mediated Zinc Extraction‐Induced Carbon Defects Boost Fe Single‐Atom Catalysis for Efficient Oxygen Reduction
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract: ABSTRACT Fe single‐atom catalysts with Fe‐N 4 configurations typically suffer from excessive adsorption of oxygenated intermediates, leading to intrinsic limitations in catalytic efficiency. Here, we propose a Bi‐mediated Fe‐adjacent Zn extraction strategy to create defects adjacent to Fe‐N 4 moieties on ZIF‐8‐derived carbon support, thereby tailoring the local microenvironment of Fe single atoms. The resulting Fe‐N‐pC d catalyst exhibits outstanding oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) activity in alkaline electrolyte, delivering a half‐wave potential of 0.918 V versus RHE along with excellent durability. The assembled quasi‐solid‐state Zn‐air battery using Fe‐N‐pC d as the air cathode catalyst affords stable operation for over 3000 h at −40°C. Mechanistic investigations demonstrate that the formed carbon defects adjacent to Fe‐N 4 sites redistribute the local electron density and favor the formation of an axial *OH‐bound Fe state under ORR conditions. This defect‐modulated coordination environment lowers the Fe d‐band center and alleviates the overly strong Fe‐*OH coupling, thereby changing the potential‐limiting step from *OH removal to *OOH formation and accelerating ORR kinetics. This study provides a neighboring‐template extraction route for engineering defect microenvironments adjacent to metal single atoms, opening new opportunities for the design of efficient ORR electrocatalysts.

title: Absolute quantification and profiling of cellular tRNAs by nanopore sequencing and a deep learning classifier
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transfer RNAs (tRNAs) link mRNA codons to amino acids during translation. Their abundance and modification states are dynamically regulated and influence translation efficiency, mRNA stability, and proteostasis. Accurate profiling of tRNAs is essential, but deep sequencing suffers from modification-induced biases during cDNA synthesis, while nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) still faces challenges in accurate tRNA profiling. Here, we develop an end-to-end deep learning model, termed nano tRNA classifier, that directly uses nanopore-DRS ionic current signals to classify tRNAs without basecalling. The model achieves 98.2% classification accuracy with high read retention across all Escherichia coli tRNA species. Using an equimolar mixture of native tRNAs as a ground-truth reference, we correct read-count bias, enabling absolute quantification and profiling under diverse culture conditions. We further develop binary classifiers that detect specific tRNA modifications at the single-molecule level with high accuracy. This nanopore-based platform integrates accurate tRNA classification, absolute quantification, and single-molecule modification detection.

title: Multifunctional Cross-Linked Micelles for the Treatment of Acute Pneumonia Caused by MDR-KP with Reduced Cytokine Storms and Restored Metabolism and Immune Balance
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Acute pneumonia caused by multidrug-resistant superbugs such as Klebsiella pneumoniae (MDR-KP) poses a severe public health threat for clinical patients with high mortality rate, where excessive cytokine storms and cellular dysfunction are the leading causes of death. More seriously, these superbugs have evolved specialized biological mechanisms that allow them to persist long-term within macrophages, rendering antibiotics and immunomodulators ineffective. Herein, a smart and multifunctional nanomicelle (NAC151-micelle), composed of colistin-NAD+-crosslinked drug and inhibitor H151, is developed for cooperatively killing of MDR-KP bacteria, alleviating hyperinflammatory cytokine storm, and improving metabolism and immune balance. NAC151-micelles optimized through in vitro bactericidal assays can smartly be responsive to the highly reduced environment within infected macrophages, allowing rapid release of active cargoes, including colistin and NAD+, thereby achieving efficient clearance of extra- and intracellular MDR-KP while improving cellular energy metabolism. Meanwhile, co-loaded H151 can cooperatively downregulate key inflammatory pathways of STING-TBK1-IRF3 and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation in macrophages with NAD+, reducing a cytokine storm. In MDR-KP-induced acute pneumonia infection, following intranasal tracheal administration, we observe a targeted accumulation in lung and significant downregulation of MDR-KP burden, together with drastically decreased cytokine storms with good safety. Furthermore, the immune balance in the lung is also greatly improved; pathological tissue injury is effectively repaired; and notably, functional macrophages are essential mediators of their therapeutic efficacy. Collectively, our study presents a safe and multifunctional therapeutic strategy (NAC151-micelles) for acute pneumonia caused by super-bacteria MDR-KP with rapid bacterial clearance, reduced cytokine storms, and improved metabolism and immune balance.

title: Evidence and measures of the digital usage divide from 40 million Windows devices
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Digital infrastructure is crucial for economic opportunities, social inclusion, and civic participation, but benefits remain unevenly distributed. Existing measures, such as computer ownership and broadband adoption, do not capture the depth and variety of digital use. We develop measures using Microsoft telemetry collected during operating system updates from 40 million Windows devices in U.S. households. These measures provide greater coverage and granularity than existing commercial or government surveys. Device representations at the ZIP-code level reveal substantial variation in usage, including an urban-rural divide and disparities within narrowly defined Metropolitan Statistical Areas. Income and education correlate with these differences. These effects are large and suggest that digital usage gaps extend beyond the local availability of essential IT infrastructure. The findings call for interventions that complement infrastructure access with support for technology use and skills development. The resulting indices are publicly available to support future research on digital inequality.

title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts as architects of tumor immune geography and lymphoid organization
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) shape how immune cells are organized within tumors and either support or hinder the formation of immune niches associated with clinical outcomes and treatment response known as tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs). Some CAF states support immune-cell recruitment and TLS establishment, whereas others create dense, fibrotic environments that restrict immune organization. Importantly, the presence of TLSs does not by itself indicate antitumor immunity. Their function depends on surrounding CAFs, extracellular matrix, and blood and lymphatic vessels. In this Review, we argue that the TLS-CAF axis is a key determinant of antitumor immunity, highlighting a potential therapeutic opportunity for selective stromal reprogramming.

title: Correlative nanoscale chemical imaging reveals delocalized Faradaic processes at isolated MXene flakes
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides (MXenes) combine an electrochemically active surface with high conductivity and hydrophilicity, which makes them a unique class of materials for electrochemical applications. While the pseudocapacitive behaviour of MXenes in acidic environments is relatively well understood on macroscale electrodes, intrinsic electrochemical phenomena occurring on single MXene flakes remain unclear. Here, we use scanning X-ray microscopy (SXM) to correlate the electronic structure of Ti3C2Tx MXene flakes at the nanoscale with local electrochemical reactions triggered at the sub-flake level by scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM). For several proton-coupled electron transfer reactions, including electrochemical oxidation and the hydrogen evolution reaction, we demonstrate a delocalization of the reactions well beyond the MXene flake area in contact with the droplet cell. Furthermore, we show evidence of hydrogen storage on monolayer MXene flakes. This work highlights fundamental insights into the role of interfacial water on surface redox reactions.

title: Effect of NBI on thermal quench dynamics in TCV disruptions
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: A neutral beam injection (NBI) heat deposition model is implemented in the Disruption Runaway Electron Analysis Model (Dream), accounting for the attenuation of the neutral beam particles, the resulting beam shine-through, and the partition of deposited energy between electrons and ions. The NBI model is applied to three TCV disruption discharges (# , # , and # ) with different amounts of injected NBI power, and bayesian inference is used to constrain the heat transport and neon injection parameters. Sets of parameters are found which allow the simulations to reproduce the experimentally measured electron temperature, radiated power, and initial line-integrated density. The final runaway electron density is shown to be only weakly affected by NBI, and further comparisons between fluid and kinetic simulations indicate that a slight reduction in early runaway generation can be followed by enhanced runaway production at later times. Extrapolation to ITER also suggests that unrealistically large NBI powers would be required to produce a comparable effect. These results indicate that NBI can affect disruption dynamics in small and medium-size tokamaks, but is insufficient to affect the thermal quench dynamics in reactor-scale tokamaks.

title: Enhanced laser-driven directional neutron source via Bayesian optimization of cone targets
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: Laser-driven neutron sources, particularly beam-target neutron sources, hold significant potential for applications in neutron radiography, non-destructive inspection, nuclear astrophysics, etc. However, the quality of current beam-target neutron sources, especially neutron yield and divergence angle, still requires substantial improvement. Here, we present a novel laser-driven cone-target scheme to enhance the quality of neutron beams. Through integrated two-dimensional (2D) particle-in-cell (PIC) and Monte Carlo (MC) simulations, it is demonstrated that the proposed scheme significantly enhances the ion acceleration by effectively focusing the laser pulse and guiding the electron beams. With the resulting increase in ion energy, a number of neutrons per laser shot of about is achieved, which is 39 times higher than that from the plane target. Moreover, the scheme raises the forward-to-sideward yield ratio and makes the emission of the high-energy neutrons more forward-directed. Our theoretical model systematically elucidates the physical mechanisms governing high-energy ion generation, neutron yield enhancement and forward-emission optimization. Assisted by Bayesian optimization, the influences of the target and laser parameters are also investigated and the optimal parameter ranges are identified, facilitating the experimental demonstration of laser-driven directional neutron sources.

title: The bootstrap current in the standard and strongly inward-shifted LHD configurations in the 1/ν and plateau regimes
source: Nuclear Fusion - latest papers
abstract: While a tokamak has a plasma current disruption, a helical system is much more robust because the current-less operation is, in principle, possible. However, a bootstrap (BS) current due to the pressure gradient could be a concern because it could change the rotational transform. We conducted experiments on the BS current in the Large Helical Device (LHD) in the 1/ν and plateau regimes using three magnetic axis configurations Rax = 3.75 m, 3.6 m and 3.53 m with completely balanced neutral beam injection (NBI). As a reference, we use the standard configuration of Rax = 3.75 m. We then examine the inward-shifted configuration of Rax = 3.6 m, and the strongly inward-shifted configuration of Rax = 3.53 m, which is referred to the neoclassically optimized configuration (Murakami et al 2002 J. Plasma Fusion Res. 5 620;, Murakami et al 2002 Nucl. Fusion42 L19). It was demonstrated that the BS current for Rax = 3.53 m is clearly lower than that for Rax = 3.75 m, together with a confinement improvement. Based on these experimental results, the BS current coefficient has been derived, which helps to predict the BS current in a helical fusion reactors.

title: SimPoly: Simulation of polymers with machine learning force fields derived from first principles
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polymers are a versatile class of materials with widespread industrial applications. Advanced computational tools could revolutionize their design, but the complex, multi-scale nature of polymers poses significant modeling challenges. Classical force fields often lack the accuracy and transferability that polymers demand, while quantum-chemical methods are prohibitively expensive for the large systems and long timescales involved. Here we develop a fast, scalable machine learning force field and show that, trained on quantum-chemical calculations alone, without any experimental data, it predicts measured bulk properties across a broad range of polymers. It reproduces polymer densities as accurately as, or better than, established classical force fields and captures the glass transition signature in the density-temperature curve, enabling the prediction of glass transition temperatures. To accelerate progress in this domain, we release a benchmark of experimental bulk properties for 130 polymers and an accompanying quantum-chemical dataset, laying the foundation for a fully in silico design pipeline for next-generation polymeric materials.
