title: Room-temperature fabrication of 2D nanomaterials
source: Matter
abstract: Two-dimensional nanomaterials are usually made at high temperatures, which is costly and hard to scale up. This review compares room-temperature exfoliation methods that peel layered crystals into ultrathin sheets, examining their yields, defect levels, and flake sizes. It proposes reporting standards and a decision flowchart to help researchers choose the right method for a given application and highlights hybrid processes, real-time monitoring, and AI-driven optimization as promising routes toward industrial production.

title: Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity
source: Nature
abstract: Tumour cells evade detection and elimination by the immune system through a suite of adaptations1, including the repression of antigen presentation, which is required for the recognition of tumour cells by CD8+ T cells. Mitochondria have emerged as targets for enhancing antitumour immunity; however, the extensive mitochondrial proteome has remained largely unstudied for its ability to modulate immune responses. Here we show that defects in the mitochondrial protein import machinery promote tumour immunogenicity and synergize with immune checkpoint blockade treatment in melanoma models. Mitochondrial protein import perturbation, specifically through depletion of the TIM23 import complex subunit TIMM50, enhances tumour immunogenicity through a pathway involving mitochondrial DNA escape, cGAS-STING pathway activation and interferon-β (IFNβ) secretion. Secreted IFNβ signals through the type I IFN receptor to activate the JAK-STAT pathway, resulting in increased antigen presentation on MHC class I complexes. Mitochondrial DNA escape in Timm50-depleted cells is linked to the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles. Depletion of SNX9 and RAB9, involved in mitochondrial-derived vesicle formation2, suppresses mitochondrial DNA-dependent type I IFN production and signalling. By disrupting mitochondrial proteostasis and membrane architecture, defective protein import in Timm50-depleted cells drives the immune phenotype. This study shows that mitochondrial protein import inhibition causes tumour immunogenicity, including sensitization to immune checkpoint blockade, by promoting mitochondrial DNA escape and IFNβ-driven MHC class I antigen presentation.

title: Metasurface waveguides for all-day augmented reality glasses
source: Nature
abstract: Augmented reality (AR) displays, originating from early optical see-through head-mounted systems1, have evolved towards lightweight glasses that seamlessly integrate digital information with the physical world2,3. However, their widespread adoption requires compact optical systems that enable bright, wide-field and comfortable viewing. Diffractive waveguides (WGs) offer a promising approach towards lightweight AR displays yet face inherent trade-offs among field of view (FoV), optical efficiency and eyebox size owing to limited degrees of freedom in light control. Here we show an all-day-wearable AR glass prototype based on spatially varying, interwoven metasurfaces that provide several grating vectors for multidirectional light control. The resulting dual-layer metasurface-based waveguide (meta-WG) achieves a 30° FoV and an 8 × 8-mm2 two-dimensional (2D) eyebox while maintaining an average luminance efficiency of 1,938 nits lm-1 (up to 4,225 nits lm-1) within a 1.5-mm-thick form factor. The prototype produces bright and stable virtual images under outdoor ambient illumination, demonstrating the compatibility of meta-WGs with practical wearable display requirements. By expanding the degrees of freedom for light routing beyond conventional diffractive WGs, our approach provides a scalable framework for balancing efficiency, viewing range and form factor, bringing high-performance AR glasses closer to practical consumer applications.

title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Accessing reversible four-electron iodine redox chemistry in aqueous metal–iodine batteries offers a promising route towards high-energy aqueous energy storage, but has conventionally relied on highly concentrated, corrosive halogen-containing electrolytes to stabilize reactive hypervalent iodine cations through interhalogen complexation
                    1–9
                    . Here we show a kosmotropic anion–polar anion–nucleophilic species (Nuc) electrolyte framework that harnesses anionic chemistry to coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions, enabling reversible four-electron iodine conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes. Polar anions establish a water-deficient, anion-enriched interfacial microenvironment, whereas kosmotropic anions regulate water–Nuc interactions to increase the availability of Nuc for stabilizing hypervalent iodine cations through Nuc–I
                    +
                    –Nuc halogen bonds. This electrolyte framework is validated across diverse Nuc and in both aqueous Zn–I
                    2
                    and Al–I
                    2
                    batteries. Moving beyond conventional interhalogen stabilization, these findings establish a distinct electrolyte chemistry framework and represent a mechanistic shift for reversible multi-electron iodine chemistry in aqueous environments.

title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Brown adipocytes (BAs) are thermogenic cells that regulate energy homeostasis, and age-related declines in thermogenesis contribute to cold sensitivity
                    1–5
                    . We previously identified a BA subpopulation with low UCP1 expression (hereafter, BA-L cells) that coexists with the classical, high-UCP1-expressing BAs (hereafter, BA-H cells)
                    6
                    . Here we show that IL-1β secreted by neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby BAs in the BA-L state. Specifically, IL-1β stabilizes hexose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (H6PD) protein from degradation to ensure the generation of active glucocorticoids, which activate the glucocorticoid receptor (GR, encoded by
                    Nr3c1
                    ) and increase the expression of its target gene, regulator of G-protein signalling 2 (
                    Rgs2
                    ), thereby suppressing UCP1 expression. Cold exposure reduces IL-1β levels, depending on sympathetic innervation, leading to H6PD degradation and the conversion of BA-L cells to BA-H cells, thereby enhancing UCP1-dependent thermogenesis. Rising environmental temperatures trigger the opposite events. BA-specific inducible deletion of
                    Nr3c1
                    during cold exposure locks these cells in the BA-H state, leading to persistent thermogenesis and increased energy expenditure days after the mice return to room temperature. Notably, IL-1β is elevated in aged brown adipose tissue, resulting in a locked low BA-H/BA-L ratio and cold intolerance. Suppressing GR in aged mice restores the BA-H/BA-L ratio, resumes thermogenesis and increases energy expenditure. Our findings reveal a spatiotemporal neuronal–immune regulation of BA heterogeneity that governs thermogenesis and offers a fundamental understanding of the mechanisms underlying increased cold sensitivity in older individuals.

title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis
source: Nature
abstract: Breast cancer, the most diagnosed cancer among women, is stratified by gene expression patterns into luminal and basal-like subtypes, and the latter is associated with worse prognosis1-3. Recent advances in single-cell technologies have underscored the presence of intratumour heterogeneity, which poses substantial challenges in cancer treatment and achieving long-term disease-free survival4-7. Here we extensively profile epigenetic heterogeneity in a cohort of treatment-naive human luminal tumours, which were obtained directly after surgical resection. By applying a single-cell epigenetic approach based on cytometry by time-of-flight, we identify a recurrent subpopulation of basal-like cells in luminal tumours with a conserved epigenetic signature across patients. These basal-like cells, also identified by deconvolution of whole-genome DNA methylation patterns, are characterized by high expression of aggressive oncogenic traits and downregulation of hormone receptor signalling. Direct comparison of single-cell proteomic and genomic profiling of monomethylation and trimethylation of histone 3 on lysine 4 revealed that these marks are key features associated with loss of luminal identity. Finally, we highlight the potential of concomitant single-molecule profiling of histone modifications on cell-free nucleosomes in blood as an epigenetic liquid biopsy approach for early diagnosis of breast cancer. Moreover, the epigenetic basal signature measured in blood is linked to prognosis, which enables the identification of patients at increased risk for disease relapse.

title: A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2′,3′-cNMP produced by insect effectors
source: Nature
abstract: RNA-derived 2',3'-cyclophosphate-terminated nucleotides act as immune signalling molecules in prokaryotes and eukaryotes1-3, but how plants perceive them remains unknown. Sucking insects inject digestive enzymes including RNases into the host plant to acquire nutrients. Here we demonstrate that NIB1, a glycine-rich RNA-binding protein in rice, senses 2',3'-cyclic nucleotide monophosphates (2',3'-cNMPs; 2',3'-cAMP and 2',3'-cGMP) and adenylyl-(3'→5')-guanosine 2',3'-cyclic phosphate (ApG>p) produced by a salivary T2 ribonuclease of green stink bug during feeding. Binding of the RNase products promotes formation of nuclear condensates containing NIB1, which recruit the core immune regulator Enhanced Disease Susceptibility 1 (EDS1) and activate defence, potentially contributing to the immune signalling of Toll/interleukin-1 receptor (TIR) proteins that also produce the nuclease products. Exogenous application of 2',3'-cAMP, 2',3'-cGMP or ApG>p elicits NIB1 and EDS1-mediated immune responses. Our findings unveil a conserved pathway in plants, in which glycine-rich RNA-binding proteins perceive the nuclease-generated second messengers to launch defence and point to a potential link between plant TIR nuclease activity and EDS1 signalling.

title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The global transition towards sustainable energy systems has identified tidal power as a uniquely predictable and substantial renewable energy resource
                    1
                    . However, the highly unsteady sea environment subjects turbines to severe hydrodynamic loads, greatly increasing capital and maintenance costs
                    2,3
                    . Large-scale state-of-the-art turbines at present rely on complex, expensive active pitch systems to mitigate these fluctuations. Here we present a reliable, passive alternative: flexible rubber blades featuring chordwise trailing-edge deformation. We experimentally demonstrate that these flexible blades achieve an equivalent total energy yield over simulated tidal cycles compared with rigid blades with active pitch control, while mitigating high-frequency fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third. This passive load regulation arises from aeroelastic deformation that flattens blade camber under load, enabling structural robustness without added mechanical complexity. These findings suggest that chordwise-flexible blades can enhance the durability and performance of tidal turbines, offering a promising pathway towards more reliable and cost-effective tidal energy generation.

title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
source: Nature
abstract: The scarcity of terrestrial rocks older than 3.9 billion years (Gyr) has hindered our understanding of Earth's early evolution, fuelling persistent debates on how and when the first continental crust formed and plate tectonics started. At present, the only unequivocally documented >3.9-Gyr-old rocks are from the Acasta Gneiss Complex, Canada1-3. Here we report a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, North China Craton, in which primary magmatic zircon records elevated δ18O values (average +6.77 ± 0.23‰) and positive εHf(t) values (weighted mean +1.45 ± 0.27). This suggests a low-temperature altered basaltic source that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean. In contrast to the low-pressure origin inferred for the roughly 4.0-Gyr-old Idiwhaa unit in Acasta2, the 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss reported here exhibits geochemical signatures attributed to a high-pressure origin4. Thermodynamic and trace element modelling demonstrate that its parental magma formed by means of low-degree (8-16%) melting of basaltic crust at >1.6 GPa and 740-820 °C, suggesting rapid burial of (near-)surface-altered oceanic crust to mantle depths along a cool thermal gradient. We propose that this rapid burial was most likely achieved through a transient subduction event.

title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Plastic pollution is a defining feature of the Anthropocene
                    1
                    , and microplastics are dispersed by air and water into even remote terrestrial habitats
                    2–7
                    , yet the ecological and landscape-level processes that shape microplastic accumulation in terrestrial ecosystems remain poorly understood. Human land-use change is rapidly transforming landscapes worldwide, but the influence of this expanding human footprint on the microplastic burdens in wildlife remains largely unknown. This knowledge gap is particularly pressing in regions that are facing escalating environmental pressures, such as Brazil. Here we pair in vivo microplastic measurements with high-resolution tracking data from lowland tapirs and giant anteaters across Brazil and show that the microplastic burdens carried by free-ranging mammals increase with both the magnitude of their human footprint exposure and their proximity to development and waste management infrastructure. Microplastics were also detected in the blood of individuals occupying seemingly pristine habitats far from development, suggesting that direct exposure to human-modified landscapes is unlikely to be the sole driver of systemic microplastic burdens. In a period of accelerating global land-use change, these findings reveal how individual habitat use and anthropogenic land-use change interact to shape wildlife exposure to microplastics and suggest that managing animals’ proximity to development and waste management infrastructure may reduce the microplastic burdens carried by terrestrial wildlife.

title: Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice
source: Nature
abstract: Nuclei in early mammalian embryos undergo epigenetic reprogramming that enables the zygote to develop into a complete organism. Whereas changes in chromatin state during this critical transition period have been extensively studied1-3, changes in the nucleus that houses chromatin remain poorly understood. Here, using direct organelle capture and biophysical manipulation methods, we find that nuclei attain profound softness and plasticity during the two-cell embryonic stage in mice, facilitating major zygotic gene activation. The prominent nuclear deformability is attributable to the rapid clearance of lamin B1 from the nuclear envelope by the autophagy factor LC3. Nuclear stiffening by lamin B1 retention or its overloading results in incomplete activation of zygotic genes and impaired development. However, embryos that maintain nuclear deformability escape from this transcriptional interference. High-resolution microscopy and sequential three-dimensional fluorescence in situ hybridization analyses revealed an accumulation of active RNA polymerase II and coordinated positioning of key genomic loci near the deformable nuclear envelope. An engineered molecular tether that stiffens the nuclei restricts these nuclear activities and suppresses expression of key zygotic gene activation genes. Together, our study identifies a distinct physical nuclear state that embryos acquire at the beginning of life that supports the initiation of the zygotic transcription program.

title: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti
source: Nature
abstract: Extreme climatic events are increasing in frequency and intensity with climate change1. Their effects on species' distributions and extinction risk remain poorly understood2-9. Most species distribution models rely on long-term mean climate, overlooking potentially important nonlinear effects of extremes. Here we integrate new spatial data on severe drought10, including compounding effects of warmer temperatures, with a comprehensive curated dataset of cactus occurrences (648,316 records) and species distribution models to assess how severe drought alters projected suitable climatic area for 993 species of Cactaceae, a highly threatened family11 that is commonly considered drought tolerant. In 91% of cases, models including severe drought were better supported than mean-climate models. Across emissions scenarios (Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) SSP1-2.6 to SSP5-8.5) with 100-km dispersal, including severe drought increased the share of species losing suitable climatic area from 58-61% to 69-72%. The proportion of species projected to lose over a quarter of suitable area increased from 26-43% to 55-58%, and the proportion projected to lose over four-fifths increased from 1-15% to 25-35%. With severe drought, restricting dispersal from 100 to 0 km increased the share losing suitable area from 69-72% to 84-85% across SSPs. These declines reduced regional richness, with five bioregions potentially losing over 25% of species. These findings demonstrate that accounting for climatic extremes can alter assessments of biodiversity vulnerability under climate change. Integrating climatic extremes into ecological forecasting will be critical for assessing biodiversity loss and designing effective conservation strategies across taxa and ecosystems.

title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Somatic evolution in ageing tissues underlies many cancers
                    1,2
                    . However, our quantitative understanding of the rules governing this pre-cancerous evolution remains incomplete. Here we exploit a unique collection of serial blood samples
                    3
                    , collected annually for up to a decade and beginning as early as 15 years before diagnosis of acute myeloid leukaemia, to provide a quantitative description of pre-cancerous evolutionary dynamics. Using deep duplex sequencing and evolutionary theory, we quantify the acquisition ages and fitness effects of the key driver events in acute myeloid leukaemia development. The first driver mutations are typically acquired in the first few decades of life, when the blood remains highly polyclonal. These early slow-growing clones subsequently acquire multiple further driver mutations that confer selective advantages up to 100-fold larger than the early drivers. These faster-growing clones harbouring multiple driver mutations can cause complete somatic sweeps of the blood decades before diagnosis, a feature strongly associated with future acute myeloid leukaemia. Our data show that the clonal dynamics of blood are consistent with a set of remarkably simple evolutionary rules that strike a balance between chance and determinism.

title: Scale-rich network-based metamaterials
source: Nature
abstract: Materials, at their essence, are networks defined by homogeneity: uniform bonds, fixed thicknesses and discrete length scales. Mechanical metamaterials, while representing structurally more diverse microstructures, remain defined by the homogeneity of their unit cells, pore sizes or repeating features1,2. In contrast, as network science has revealed, real-world and biological systems—from the Internet to the brain—derive their function from broad, multiscale variability in connectivity and link length3, 4, 5–6. Here we introduce scale-rich metamaterials, a design framework that embeds network heterogeneity into mechanical metamaterials, achieving orders-of-magnitude heterogeneity in ligament lengths, thicknesses and connectivity. Governed by only two parameters, scale-rich networks span orders of magnitude in structural features, overcoming previous constraints in metamaterial design. Translating these network models into physically realizable materials, we use simulations and experiments to show that scale-rich metamaterials exhibit properties inaccessible to traditional single-scale systems, including highly tunable elastic anisotropy, delocalized nonlinear deformation with high energy absorption, enhanced energy dissipation under dynamic loading and programmable elastic-wave control. This network-based framework establishes a minimal and universal model for engineering multifunctional materials whose mechanical behaviour emerges directly from scale diversity, and also opens avenues of enquiry for network science itself. A network-science-based framework that embeds network heterogeneity into mechanical metamaterials is used to produce scale-rich metamaterials that exhibit properties inaccessible to traditional single-scale systems.

title: The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL
source: Nature
abstract: Eukaryotic genomes are exposed to numerous sources of DNA damage that impede replication. Only a decade ago, repriming by the primase-polymerase PRIMPOL was identified as a pathway that enables cells to tolerate DNA damage1-4. However, the molecular mechanism that underlies repriming remains poorly understood, and it is unclear how PRIMPOL is precisely targeted to stalled forks, where along single-stranded DNA PRIMPOL binds and how PRIMPOL is regulated to minimize error-prone DNA synthesis. Here, to dissect the molecular basis of repriming, we perform real-time single-molecule imaging in nuclear extracts that recapitulate genome maintenance. We directly visualize how stalled forks restart through repriming. We show that PRIMPOL is recruited to stalled forks through an interaction with the replicative helicase CDC45-MCM2-7-GINS (CMG). This facilitates primer handover from PRIMPOL to the high-fidelity polymerase ε, minimizing mutagenic DNA synthesis. At near-physiological concentrations, PRIMPOL reprimes leading strands in a CMG-dependent manner and polymerase ε extends those primers. This primary mode of repriming does not require DNA damage checkpoint signalling. PRIMPOL overexpression and checkpoint activation promote a secondary mode of repriming, whereby PRIMPOL restarts DNA synthesis far from CMG and polymerase δ extends those primers. Our data reveal a simple yet effective mechanism that directs PRIMPOL's activity to stalled forks awaiting restart, and suggest a strategy to inhibit the repriming pathway.

title: Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Transcriptional addiction to the androgen receptor (AR) underlies metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer
                    1
                    , in which AR maintains oncogenic programs through domain-specific interactions with the acetyltransferases p300 and CBP (collectively p300/CBP)
                    2
                    . Here we describe a novel therapeutic modality, domain-alteration chimeras (DALTACs), that rewire endogenous protein complexes by enforcing non-native domain–domain interactions. Our first-in-class AR–p300/CBP DALTAC-1 induces synthetic proximity between the ligand-binding domain of AR and the bromodomain of p300/CBP, misconfiguring their native interface and locking the complex in a non-productive state. DALTAC-1 triggers a ‘super-inhibitory’ effect, suppressing AR-driven transcription and proliferation more potently than combined AR and p300/CBP inhibition. Mechanistically, DALTAC-1 reprograms p300/CBP substrate engagement, abolishing the histone mark H2B N-terminal acetylation and inducing neomorphic acetylation of AR and coactivators, ultimately collapsing the AR neo-enhanceosome. Chromatin profiling revealed redistribution of AR and p300/CBP towards palindromic androgen response elements, accompanied by disruption of cofactor and transcriptional machinery recruitment at oncogenic AR and ERG neo-enhancers. DALTAC-1 exhibits exquisite lineage selectivity, displaying potent activity in AR–p300/CBP dual-dependent cells and sparing AR-negative cells. In multiple in vivo models, DALTAC-1 induces deep and durable tumour regressions. Together, these findings establish DALTACs as a broadly applicable strategy to rewire disease-defining complexes through domain-topology alteration, expanding induced-proximity therapies, and the precise lineage selectivity of DALTAC-1 supports its translational potential in AR-driven prostate cancer.

title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    The nuclear pore complex (NPC) regulates molecular traffic between nucleus and cytoplasm
                    1,2
                    . Its permeability barrier is formed by intrinsically disordered phenylalanine-glycine-rich nucleoporins (FG-NUPs), whose physical state has long been debated
                    3–13
                    . Deciphering how FG-NUPs behave inside living cells is crucial for understanding how NPCs achieve both selective and rapid transport. By combining site-specific labelling with time-resolved fluorescence anisotropy, here we show that FG domains exhibit nanosecond-scale, liquid-like segmental motion in live cells, whereas reconstituted FG condensates undergo a liquid-to-solid transition in vitro. Experiments and molecular-dynamics simulations further show that importin-β, a principal nuclear transport receptor, and O-linked β-
                    N
                    -acetylglucosamine, a key post-translational modification of FG-NUPs, together stabilize the dynamic FG network. Finely balanced FG–FG and FG–importin-β interactions maintain FG-NUP liquidity and generate a radial organization in which importin-β is enriched near the NPC periphery and extended FG domains remain in the central channel, forming the transport barrier. This organization explains recent MINFLUX observations
                    14
                    of rim-biased transport trajectories and is supported here by direct MINFLUX imaging of importin-β in mammalian cells. Together, our results reconcile conflicting models of FG-NUP organization
                    4,5,7,9,15
                    and establish a framework for understanding how cellular context tunes intrinsically disordered proteins in health and disease.

title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints
                    1,2
                    . Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability
                    3
                    . Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
source: Nature
abstract: Immunoglobulin A (IgA) is the most abundant antibody isotype produced by mammals, and has a specialized role in mucosal homeostasis1. IgA is constantly secreted into the intestinal lumen and binds to commensal microorganisms to regulate their colonization and function2,3, with unclear implications for health. IgA deficiency is common in humans, but difficult to study, because of its complex aetiology and comorbidities4-8. Here we use genetically and environmentally controlled mice to show that various models of IgA deficiency result in increased susceptibility to several models of endogenous colorectal cancer. Cellular and molecular analyses revealed that, in the absence of IgA, colonic epithelial cells induce antibacterial factors and accelerate cell cycling in response to the microbiota. Oral treatment with IgA was sufficient to reduce steady-state proliferation and protect mice from tumours; however, this function was due to the structure of the antibody rather than to binding specificity. In a reductionist culture system, IgA directly suppressed epithelial growth. Co-immunoprecipitation mass spectrometry and targeted CRISPR screening identified DMBT1 as an IgA-binding epithelial surface protein that is required for IgA-mediated suppression of proliferation. Together, IgA and DMBT1 tune the normal cycling of absorptive colonocyte progenitors. In IgA-knockout mice, deleting the transmembrane and cytoplasmic signalling portions of DMBT1 was sufficient to reverse both the increased epithelial cell proliferation and the increased tumour susceptibility seen in these mice. These experiments establish a homeostatic function for IgA in tempering physiological epithelial responses to the microbiota to maintain mucosal health.

title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
source: Nature
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    A new epoch for direct visualization of accretion dynamics near the event horizon of a black hole began when the Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration synthesized an Earth-sized aperture with millimetre radio interferometry and published the first reconstructed image
                    1–4
                    of a black hole shadow at the core of radio galaxy Messier 87 (M87). The image appeared as a ring-like structure, representing the gravitationally lensed and redshifted emission around the central supermassive black hole, M87*, located at the galactic nucleus. However, application of various data analysis and imaging heuristics resulted in divergent representations of M87* fine-scale features
                    3,5–7
                    , with some external analyses even challenging the fundamental ring-like morphology of the source
                    8,9
                    . Such difficulties arise as a consequence of the inherent sparsity of the very long baseline interferometry measurements, making interferometric image reconstruction an inadequately constrained problem. Moreover, the solution is sensitive to instrument calibration, post-processing algorithms and imaging hyperparameters. Here we apply an independent imaging algorithm that we have developed to the M87* dataset that is free from prescriptive morphological priors and founded on observables immune to instrument calibration errors. We reconstruct the black hole shadow image and unequivocally reproduce a ring-like morphology, with an angular diameter of 42.2 ± 1.5 μas corresponding to a black hole mass of 6.5 ± 0.5 billion solar masses assuming nominal scaling parameters, observed at an inclination angle of approximately 20° from the approaching jet.

title: Neuromelanin-inspired metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks restore neuronal excitability in radiation-induced brain injury
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Radiation-induced brain injury (RIBI) affects up to 30% of patients receiving cranial radiotherapy, representing an irreversible complication lacking effective therapies. Research advances are limited by poor blood-brain barrier drug penetration and overreliance on ex vivo pathology, which cannot resolve dynamic neuronal dysfunction. Inspired by neuromelanin, we fabricated metal-selenomelanin nanonetworks (MSMNs), combined with in vivo electrophysiology to investigate and mitigate radiation-triggered neural dysfunction. In 6-gray whole body–irradiated mice, MSMN normalized neuronal excitability and restored medium spiny neuron firing and striatal circuit activity, improving locomotor and anxiety-related behaviors. Besides central functional recovery, MSMN provides systemic radioprotection, ensuring full 30-day survival, protecting radiosensitive organs and facilitating hematopoietic recovery. This work identifies neuronal excitability as an underexplored therapeutic target for RIBI, establishing neuromelanin-mimetic selenomelanin nanonetworks as a bioinspired platform linking molecular radioprotection to circuit-level restoration for radiation-induced neurological injury.

title: Modest loss of sleep increases susceptibility to cybersecurity threats
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Sleep restriction leads to impaired cognitive processing across domains. I examined whether the transition to daylight saving time (DST), typically accompanied by compromised sleep, would lead to an increase in the probability of falling prey to a simulated phishing attack using a fully naturalistic experiment with random assignment and blinding. A predatory email was sent to employees at the University of California, Irvine (N = 11,218) either on the morning of Monday following the transition to DST or one week earlier. The transition led to a ~13% increase in the probability of clicking a suspicious link, without affecting the probability of opening the email or reporting it as spam. These results demonstrate that even modest, mundane, and acute loss of sleep has real-life, potentially hazardous, implications for cognitive function.

title: Lipid droplets buffer hydrogen sulfide–induced redox imbalance
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The electron transport chain is a signaling hub for hydrogen sulfide (H
                    2
                    S) that serves both as a respiratory substrate and an inhibitor. While acute sulfide toxicity is well characterized, cellular adaptations to chronic H
                    2
                    S, particularly microbially-derived sulfide exposure in colon, is poorly understood. We report that chronic, low-level H
                    2
                    S exposure (4 to 20 µM) drives robust carbon sequestration in lipid droplets (LD) across several human cell lines, driven by a coordinated remodeling of redox and nucleotide metabolism. Specifically, H
                    2
                    S-induced reductive shifts in nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD) and coenzyme Q (CoQ) pools are accompanied by glycerol-3-phosphate accumulation and cytidine triphosphate (CTP) depletion. Lipidomic analysis reveals increased neutral lipid synthesis and triacylglyceride accumulation concomitant with decreased CTP-dependent synthesis of membrane phospholipids. Mitochondrial expression of a water-generating NADH oxidase attenuates LD accumulation and spatially confines the origin of H
                    2
                    S-induced reductive stress signaling to this compartment. Interestingly, LD abundance increases even after H
                    2
                    S withdrawal, continuing over 48 h, during which time the reductively-shifted NAD and CoQ pools slowly reoxidize. Inhibition of fatty acid synthesis during sulfide exposure impairs cellular recovery of respiration. These findings establish an active role for LDs in stress response and reveal that lipid biogenesis is a strategy for countering H
                    2
                    S-induced redox imbalance. The sulfide–LD–redox axis uncovered in this study has implications for understanding how gut-derived H
                    2
                    S, shaped by diet and microbiome, can influence metabolic health.

title: PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 7 moderates the activity of phytochrome A in persistent canopy shade conditions
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: In nature, plants perceive and respond to complex vegetative environments through the phytochrome (phy) photoreceptor-signaling system. The Canopy Adaptation Strategy, elicited by phyA, together with the Shade Avoidance Syndrome, regulated by phyB, enables plants to adapt to diverse forms of vegetation shade. The phyA High Irradiance Response mode, which involves photocycle-coupled nuclear shuttling, is essential for sensing sustained far-red-rich conditions typical of canopy or occlusive shade. Our research identifies PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 7 (PIF7) as a key regulator of phyA function. We show that PIF7 overexpression (PIF7ox) effectively suppresses phyA action. Under persistent shade, PIF7 and phyA both accumulate and associate within nuclear photobodies, with this interaction mediated by the C-terminal domain of PIF7 and the PAS-PAS domain of phyA. PIF7 also interacts with FAR-RED ELONGATED HYPOCOTYL 1 (FHY1) and FHY1-LIKE transport facilitators, thereby interfering with phyA cytosolic-nuclear shuttling. This coordinated molecular targeting by PIF7 constitutes an effective strategy for modulating phyA function under persistent shade conditions.

title: PPP1R1B differentially modulates alcohol intake and emotional comorbidity through distinct prefrontal circuits
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Excessive alcohol consumption frequently co-occurs with anxiety and depression in alcohol use disorder (AUD), yet the specific neural circuits and molecular mechanisms coordinating these comorbid conditions remain poorly defined. The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), particularly its prelimbic (PL) and infralimbic (IL) subregions, projects to key reward and emotion centers like the nucleus accumbens (Nac) and basolateral amygdala (BLA), but the functional heterogeneity of these projections is unclear. Using chemogenetics, retrograde tracing, electrophysiology, spatial proteomics, and cell-type-specific gene editing in mice subjected to a 4-wk intermittent access to alcohol (IAA) paradigm, we selectively manipulated glutamatergic projections from the PL and IL to the Nac core, Nac shell, and BLA and assessed alcohol intake, anxiety-like, and depression-like behaviors. Chemogenetic activation of PL-Nac core projections reduced short-term alcohol intake, anxiety-, and depression-like behaviors, while IL-BLA activation decreased alcohol consumption and anxiety-like behaviors only. Retrograde tracing revealed mirror-image anatomical segregation of projection-defined neuronal subpopulations within PL/IL linking spatial organization to functional divergence. IAA induced pathway-specific synaptic adaptations. Spatial proteomics nominated protein phosphatase 1 regulatory subunit 1B (PPP1R1B) as a candidate molecule in PL-Nac core neurons. Independent immunostaining confirmed PPP1R1B downregulation, and circuit-specific knockout recapitulated alcohol-related and affective phenotypes, whereas overexpression reversed them. In IL-BLA neurons, PPP1R1B manipulation modulated alcohol intake and anxiety, but not depression. These findings define a subregion- and projection-specific organizational logic in the mPFC for differentially regulating alcohol consumption and emotional comorbidity, with PPP1R1B as a key molecular determinant. This provides a neural pathway–molecule framework for targeted intervention in AUD.

title: RE1 silencing transcription factor is reduced in endometriosis, and uterine deletion in mice alters progesterone responsiveness
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Endometriosis is a steroid-dependent gynecologic disease characterized by progesterone (P4) resistance, subfertility/infertility, and pelvic pain; however, the molecular mechanisms underlying impaired P4 responsiveness in endometriosis tissue are not fully understood. RE1 silencing transcription factor (REST), a transcriptional regulator implicated in steroid hormone signaling, has emerged as a potential mediator of P4 responsiveness. Here, we investigated the role of REST in endometriosis using human tissues and a uterine-specific Rest conditional knockout mouse model. Immunohistochemical analysis of eutopic endometrium and ectopic lesions from patients with endometriosis revealed significantly reduced nuclear REST expression compared with control endometrium, suggesting loss of functional REST in disease. To assess the physiological consequences of REST deficiency, uterine-specific Rest knockout (Rest
                    d/d
                    ) mice were generated. Rest
                    d/d
                    females exhibited progressive subfertility and hyperestrogenic uterine tissue characteristics that displayed a blunted responsiveness to P4 treatment. Loss of Rest selectively altered expression of P4-responsive genes associated with endometriosis pathology, despite preserved P4 receptor expression. Following induction of experimental endometriosis, female mice that developed endometriotic-like lesions using Rest-deficient donor tissue developed significantly larger lesions that were less responsive to P4 treatment compared to lesions induced using control tissue. Mechanical sensitivity was modestly increased in mice receiving Rest-deficient tissue, whereas vaginal hyperalgesia was unaffected. These findings identify loss of nuclear REST as a feature of endometriosis and support a role of REST in subfertility, lesion progression, and blunted response to P4. REST may represent a molecular contributor to altered P4 responsiveness and a potential therapeutic target in endometriosis.

title: Dynamic supercoiling sponsors transcription amplification by MYC
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Dysregulated MYC provokes profound changes in cancer gene expression. Although usually considered an E-box-dependent transcription activator, an alternate model is that MYC is a universal amplifier of transcription. Although MYC participates in pause release, its full role in the transcription cycle remains poorly illuminated. MYC also stimulates topoisomerases to resolve DNA topological issues complicating its transactions; how this stimulation is coordinated with its transcriptional role has not been examined. We have developed a system that discriminates between MYC-driven activation versus amplification in any cell. This system enables the interrogation of genes, cofactors, and compounds that execute or modulate MYC activity. Using a combination of biochemical and cellular assays, we reveal dynamic interplay between MYC-driven transcription amplification and DNA supercoiling. Because the early stages of transcription are sensitive to DNA supercoiling, Reducing TOP1 activity 1 either through genetic knockdown or low-dose inhibition, potentiates transcription amplification by MYC. By increasing promoter melting and RNA polymerase loading, negative supercoiling provides the early transcription complexes upon which MYC acts to increase output.

title: Structural insights into the evolution of mitochondrial protein import from the trypanosome ATOM complex
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The translocase of the outer membrane (TOM) mediates the import of most mitochondrial preproteins. In the protozoan parasite
                    Trypanosoma brucei
                    , this machinery is replaced by the atypical translocase of the outer membrane (ATOM), whose composition differs substantially from the canonical TOM complexes of fungi and metazoans. Here, we report the cryoelectron microscopy structure of the
                    T. brucei
                    ATOM complex at 2.8 Å resolution. The structure resolves all previously identified components together with an additional, previously uncharacterized subunit. Despite its divergent composition, ATOM retains a conserved dimeric channel architecture and a protein-conducting pathway closely resembling those of opisthokont TOM complexes, indicating that the core mechanism of mitochondrial protein translocation was established early in eukaryotic evolution. In contrast, the receptor and intermembrane-space regions exhibit distinct architectures, revealing extensive evolutionary diversification and multiple examples of convergent evolution. Together, these findings provide a near-atomic view of the ATOM translocase and offer insights into the origin, conservation, and diversification of the mitochondrial protein import machinery across eukaryotes.

title: Recurrent hybridization between highly divergent paramecium species
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
The process of speciation, through which two reproductively isolated species emerge from an ancestral population, is often gradual, including a period during which gene flow still occurs, and hence speciation remains reversible. However, if isolation persists, the progressive accumulation of genetic incompatibilities ultimately locks the speciation process, reaching the point where hybrid offspring are inviable or sterile. In plants and animals, the establishment of species barriers is quite rapid: Beyond a net genetic divergence of 0.02 substitutions per synonymous site, interspecific introgressions become extremely rare. Here we report that in ciliates, species barriers can be broken despite huge genetic divergence. We show that the genome of
                    Paramecium sonneborni
                    contains hundreds of DNA segments that were acquired by recurrent horizontal transfers from multiple very distant lineages (synonymous divergence ~1 substitution/site). These segments approach the size of full-length chromosomes, which indicates that they were introgressed by interspecific mating. These data show that in the ancestry of
                    P. sonneborni
                    , hybridization events with highly divergent species occurred repeatedly and led to viable and fertile offspring. We propose that this unexpected promiscuous sexual behavior is made possible by the fact that paramecia separate somatic and germline functions in two types of nuclei: The elimination of non-self-DNA fragments during the development of the somatic genome allows individuals of a species to remain phenotypically the same, despite recurrent genetic flow from distant species into their germline.

title: Wearable interstitial fluid sensing of time-resolved uric acid for early prediction of flare-associated pain in an induced mouse model
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Gout flare is driven by hyperuricemia (HUA) and inflammatory responses to monosodium urate (MSU) crystals, yet single time-point serum uric acid (UA) measurements cannot capture the biochemical dynamics preceding flare onset or explain the timing of severe pain manifestation. Here, we present a skin-attachable interstitial fluid (ISF)-based electrochemical sensing platform for time-resolved, minimally invasive UA monitoring in a controlled, induced mouse model of gout flare-associated inflammation and pain. The platform integrates an enzyme-based UA sensor, a thin insertion electrode, and battery-free near-field communication (NFC), enabling time-resolved in vivo tracking of ISF UA dynamics. By establishing disease-stage-specific models comprising HUA, MSU-only inflammation, and gouty arthritis flare (GA flare) conditions, we separately examined metabolic and inflammatory contributions to flare-associated UA dynamics. Time-resolved ISF monitoring revealed that the GA flare group exhibited pronounced UA fluctuation patterns that were not reproduced by either condition alone. The peak timing of UA dynamics was temporally decoupled from pain-related behavioral responses, indicating that flare-associated pain onset cannot be explained by a single UA concentration. A machine learning framework using ISF UA time-series features identified predictive information preceding peak pain, whereas analyses using earlier events defined by sustained decreases in paw withdrawal threshold showed lower and event-definition-dependent performance. These findings establish time-resolved ISF UA monitoring as a framework for resolving flare-associated biochemical dynamics and evaluating subsequent pain progression in an induced mouse model.

title: Phylogenetic profiling reveals evolutionary coupling between methyltransferases and the cytoskeleton
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Methylation is a fundamental post-translational modification best understood as regulating chromatin structure and gene expression, yet there is emerging evidence that methylation also shapes cytoskeletal organization, regulating key processes such as mitosis and cell migration. Proteomic studies have revealed cytoskeletal protein methylation is widespread, however little is known about the enzymes responsible for these modifications, or their evolutionary relationship to other, better known substrates for methylation, such as chromatin. To address this question, we applied phylogenetic profiling across the complete repertoire of human methyltransferases to identify conserved functional relationships extending beyond chromatin. Unbiased clustering revealed extensive coevolution between methyltransferases and many components of the cytoskeleton, uncovering a previously unrecognized evolutionary network linking canonical chromatin regulatory enzymes to cellular structural systems. Evolutionary Trace analysis of the H3K36 methyltransferase family recovered known catalytic and regulatory domains while identifying additional evolutionarily constrained residues, suggesting previously unappreciated functional interfaces. Comparative analyses further distinguished deeply conserved methyltransferase–cytoskeletal relationships from those that emerged later during eukaryotic evolution, indicating that cytoskeletal methylation comprises both ancient and lineage-expanded regulatory programs. Leveraging these evolutionary signatures, we identified and experimentally validated a previously unrecognized association between the methyltransferase NSD3 and α-tubulin. Together, these findings reveal that methyltransferases traditionally viewed as chromatin regulators participate in an evolutionarily conserved network that coordinates nuclear and cytoskeletal functions. More broadly, they establish phylogenetic profiling as a powerful approach for discovering noncanonical activities of chromatin-associated enzymes and suggest that regulation of chromatin organization and cellular architecture evolved as interconnected processes.

title: Physiologic and pharmacologic role of the glucocorticoid receptor in germinal center B cells and plasmacytic differentiation
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
In diffuse large B cell lymphoma (DLBCL), a malignancy derived from germinal center (GC) B cells, somatic hypermutation aberrantly targets glucocorticoid receptor (GR) binding sequences in the super-enhancer (SE) of multiple oncogenes. These events abrogate GR binding and deregulate the expression of the SE-linked gene, suggesting an important role of GR in normal and transformed GC B cells. Using a GC-specific
                    Nr3c1
                    knockout mouse model and multi-omics analyses in murine and human GC B cells, here we show that, under physiological conditions, GR constitutively localizes to the nucleus, where it transcriptionally modulates signaling pathways implicated in GC homeostasis and plasmablast differentiation in part by antagonizing the repressive function of BCL6 on the plasma cell master regulators IRF4 and PRDM1. While loss of baseline GR activity led to mild GC hyperplasia and impaired plasmacytic differentiation, pharmacologic doses of glucocorticoids, a key component of DLBCL chemo-immunotherapy, were preferentially toxic to GC in a GC B cell–autonomous manner. These findings uncover a physiological role for GR in the GC reaction as well as in promoting plasmablast/plasma cell formation and provide insights into the specific activity of glucocorticoids in the treatment of DLBCL.

title: Dormancy stabilizes structured food webs
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Theory predicts that strong species interactions drive instability in large ecosystems, but strong interactions are common in nature while strong instability appears rare. This discrepancy motivates enduring interest in ecological mechanisms that limit or counteract instability. Dormancy—reversible metabolic suppression—may be one. Dormancy is a ubiquitous life history trait found in organisms ranging from bacteria to trees. Dormant individuals form “seed banks” that are temporarily disengaged from demographic processes and species interactions, creating a memory of past ecological dynamics. Seed banks can stabilize predator–prey interactions, but whether, when, and how they affect the stability of larger ecological networks is uncertain. We show that dormancy stabilizes oscillatory dynamics in a minimal mathematical model and illustrate how dormancy converts high oscillation frequency into strong restoring force. We find that dormancy can have qualitative stabilizing effects in structured food webs that undergo Hopf bifurcations and exhibit oscillatory instability, but rarely in unstructured networks or networks with symmetric (competitive or mutualistic) interactions. This classification remains accurate when only some species go dormant and drive stabilization. Our results clarify when dormancy can promote stability, indicating that it may be an important but overlooked stabilizing factor in food webs.

title: Multi-omics characterization of white matter free water reveals genetic and vascular determinants of neurological disorders
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: White matter free water (FW-WM), quantified using diffusion MRI, reflects extracellular water content and microstructural alterations within water matter, but its genetic architecture and clinical relevance remain largely uncharted. We conducted a multi-omics study integrating 42,039 individuals from the UK Biobank and Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative cohorts to characterize tract-specific FW-WM across genetic, phenotypic, and proteomic dimensions. Genome-wide association analyses identified 27 independent loci and prioritized 88 genes, which were enriched in the genomic functional elements of vascular endothelial cells, pericytes, and astrocytes. Notably, 20 loci (74%) were novel compared to conventional white matter metrics. Both genetic predisposition to higher FW-WM and imaging-derived FW-WM were associated with a spectrum of neurological disorders. Specifically, imaging-derived FW-WM showed strong associations with stroke (OR = 3.14) and dementia (OR = 4.15), while higher baseline FW-WM predicted progression from MCI to AD (HR = 2.58). Bidirectional Mendelian randomization analyses further supported genetically predicted associations between hypertension and FW-WM, which were together associated with increased risks of stroke and cognitive impairment. Integrative proteomic analyses further nominated PEAR1 and ANGL3 as candidate proteins potentially linking hypertension-related vascular processes to FW-WM variation. Together, these findings provide a multi-omics characterization of FW-WM that connects genetic susceptibility, vascular factors, and neurological outcomes, supporting FW-WM as a tract-specific imaging phenotype with potential utility for neurological risk stratification.

title: Phase transition in a dryland shrub–grass ecosystem: Emergence through local trade-offs
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Ecosystems are complex adaptive systems in which local interactions among individuals shape macroscopic phenomena such as pattern formation, multistability, and critical transitions. However, how such bottom-up interactions govern emergent behaviors and system-level complexity remains a central challenge in ecology. Phase transition theory, a classic paradigm in physics, links local interaction rules to emergent changes in macroscopic system states, offering a formal language for understanding cross-scale dynamics. Here we unite this theory with empirical evidence from dryland shrub–grass ecosystems and show that these systems exhibit three hallmarks of phase transitions. First, abrupt shifts separate different phases of deserts, shrublands, and grasslands. Second, shrublands and grasslands self-organize into Turing-like phase patterns, contrasting with homogeneous deserts. Third, special phenomena emerge near-transition threshold, including patch enlargement and abrupt decline at desert–vegetation interface, and fairy circles within the shrub–grass transition zone. Using a cellular automaton model built on a fundamental trade-off between extensive and intensive resource foraging strategies (EI trade-off), we show how kernels encoding local trade-offs integrate these seemingly disparate phenomena within a unified phase transition framework. Moreover, this EI trade-off was empirically validated through analyses of plant functional traits and spatial patterns of plant patches. These findings illustrate that dryland ecosystem dynamics reflect universal self-organization principles. Our work establishes phase-transition theory as a powerful framework for understanding, predicting, and managing complexity in dryland ecosystems, which advances the integration of complexity science with ecology, offering a pathway toward bottom-up ecosystem understanding.

title: Superoxide dismutase shapes manganese stoichiometry in Southern Ocean diatoms
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Quantifying the elemental stoichiometry of marine phytoplankton biomass is crucial for projections of primary production. In many cases, the mechanistic underpinnings of biomass stoichiometry are unclear. We combined metaproteomics, Bayesian statistical modeling, and geochemical measurements to quantify the contribution of superoxide dismutases to metal stoichiometry in natural populations of Southern Ocean diatoms. Our analyses indicate that a substantial amount of manganese (Mn) in diatoms in an Antarctic polynya can be attributed to superoxide dismutases (∼0.7 micromoles of Mn:moles of carbon; ∼20% of the total cellular Mn quota). We then used proteomic profiles of polar diatom cultures to identify environmental controls on superoxide dismutases and found that Mn limitation induces the depletion of Mn superoxide dismutases and an accompanying increase in nickel superoxide dismutase. Overall, we combined metaproteomic approaches to quantify proteome composition and connected these measurements to metal-to-carbon ratios and their responses to metal availability. Our approach provides a mechanism for directly parameterizing ecosystem-scale models with molecular measurements.

title: Passive imaging with quantum advantage
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Far-field optical imaging inevitably involves low-pass spatial filtering, limiting the resolution. Moreover, conventional imaging suppresses high spatial frequency components close to the cutoff, making them invisible under noise—particularly the shot noise arising from discrete and random nature of quantum light. Here, we propose and implement a method for reducing the effect of this noise by optically preprocessing the incoming light before detection, thereby optimizing the quantum measurement performed on it. Our scheme, termed Fourier domain division (FDD), partitions the Fourier plane into multiple regions for independent detection and subsequent post-processing for image reconstruction. By analyzing the quantum and classical Fisher information, we show that our method is advantageous with respect to direct imaging for high spatial-frequency components. As a result, the number of photons required to achieve a certain signal-to-noise ratio in the Fourier domain is reduced, thus enhancing the overall resolution in the photon-starved regime. We demonstrate our method in microscopy, achieving fivefold improvement of Fisher information on high spatial frequency components. Unlike active super-resolution methods, FDD is passive, making it broadly applicable in microscopy and other imaging scenarios, where active illumination is impractical, including astronomy and remote sensing, in the photon-starved regime. Our work establishes a general strategy for designing quantum optimized superresolution imaging systems, bridging fundamental quantum limits, practical image analysis, and computer vision applications.

title: Dynamic plasmonic imaging of electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for charge-resolved multiplex biosensing
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Multiplexed profiling of diverse biomarkers is essential for precision diagnostics, but remains challenging for label-free sensors because signals typically scale with analyte mass. Here, we present a dynamic plasmonic imaging platform based on electromechanically driven nano-oscillators for multiplexed, label-free quantification of nucleic acids, proteins, and small molecules within a unified sensing architecture. Size-encoded nanoparticles tethered to a plasmonic surface are electrically actuated to oscillate vertically within the evanescent field and tracked by distance-resolved surface plasmon resonance imaging. Molecular binding alters the effective surface charge of each nano-oscillator, modulating the electrostatic-driven forces and changing oscillation amplitude. This charge-to-motion transduction mechanism reduces dependence on molecular mass and enhances sensitivity for low–molecular weight analytes. This platform simultaneously detects microRNAs, proteins, and small molecules spanning a ∼300-fold molecular weight range within a single field of view. We further demonstrate multiplexed profiling of tumor-associated microRNAs in pretreated supernatants from patient-derived breast cancer cells across 24 clinical samples. Dynamic plasmonic nano-oscillators provide a scalable architecture for multiplex molecular diagnostics.

title: Integrating biomass production platform and identification approach for stereochemical assignment of super-carbon-chain compounds
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Super-carbon-chain compounds (SCCCs), marine long-carbon-chain polyketides featuring numerous carbon stereocenters, fall into untapped chemical space in between drug-like small molecules and biopolymers. Due to mass-material unavailability and flexible-structure complexity, the reliable stereochemical assignment of SCCCs has long remained stagnant. In this work, a modern microalgal biomass production-platform is created for pilot-scale cultivation of marine dinoflagellates to produce over 100 milligrams of minor SCCCs. The modular fragment-based identification (MFBI) approach is successfully employed to establish the relative and absolute configurations of SCCCs. As an example, 157.7 mg of a minor SCCC, named amphidiketol A, featuring a highly-flexible C
                    76
                    -linear carbon backbone and thirty-three carbon stereocenters, is obtained from
                    Amphidinium
                    sp. in our platform. Its hybrid architecture contains eleven‌ distinct modular fragments. Its relative and absolute configurations are successfully established by the MFBI approach. Collectively, an undescribed paradigm for stereochemical assignment of SCCCs is presented. Nine senescence-associated protein targets of amphidiketol A in lung cancer A549 cells are identified.

title: STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) is a pleiotropic cytokine that drives macrophage functions ranging from tissue homeostasis to inflammation, yet how STAT3 specifies these divergent outcomes remains unclear. By integrating transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling with selective STAT3 degradation, we show that STAT3 controls IL-6–induced epigenomic remodeling and restrains a latent STAT1-associated interferon program in human macrophages. Graded STAT3 chromatin recruitment scales with locus-specific H3K27ac deposition and transcriptional output across homeostatic and inflammatory programs. STAT3 degradation permits STAT1 recruitment at a subset of regulatory regions and engages a delayed amplification loop that is partially dependent on STING and type I IFN signaling. In severe COVID-19, monocytes exhibit exaggerated STAT3-associated inflammatory signatures together with attenuated STAT1-associated interferon responses, consistent with a skewed STAT3-STAT1 balance. These findings define a framework in which STAT3 calibrates IL-6–induced chromatin output while maintaining pathway fidelity by limiting STAT1 cross-talk.

title: Principles of use of tensile J-curve materials in antagonistic arrangements
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract: Natural ligaments are soft connective tissues that provide high stretchability for dexterous flexibility but switch to high stiffness to protect the musculoskeletal system from excessive deformation. These two functions cannot be independently tuned in conventional engineering materials with linear or hyperelasticity. Biological materials achieve this tailored behavior through a highly nonlinear tensile response characterized by a J-shaped curve, featuring an extended “toe region” of low force up to intermediate strains followed by an inflection, called the “heel region” which marks the onset of nonlinear stiffening. Here, we aim to study the characteristics of J-curves to establish principles for their use in robotic mechanisms. We define and measure the J-curve features responsible for protectiveness and mobility, describe the effective stiffness and the level of nonlinearity as a function of pre-stretch, and elucidate how the J-curve decouples flexibility from damage protection. Experimental measurements reveal the performance advantages of twisted and coiled elastomeric J-curve materials in engineered antagonistic arrangements and highlight their unique design space compared with linear elastic systems. Furthermore, we present a conceptual analysis of exploiting J-curve materials in energy-efficient running as an outlook toward their use in bioinspired robots.

title: Intermittent Cauchy walks enable optimal 3D search across target shapes and sizes
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Efficiently locating rare targets requires balancing the exploration of novel space with the exploitation of local vicinities. While this tradeoff is well documented in simplified environments, its behavior in realistic three-dimensional environments remains unclear. Here, we analyze intermittent Lévy walks in three dimensions and show that search efficiency becomes strongly dependent on target geometry, with volume, surface area, and elongation governing performance across the Lévy spectrum. title: A primordial heavy water reservoir in the outer solar system
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The oxygen (O) isotopic composition of outer solar system ices is believed to be enriched in heavy O isotopes owing to photochemical processes, but evidence for this O reservoir is exceedingly rare in meteorites. Hydrated interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) collected in Earth’s stratosphere that display high densities of solar energetic particle tracks originate from Edgeworth-Kuiper belt objects. Their mineralogy is dominated by hydrated minerals that formed by alteration of anhydrous precursor minerals at low temperatures through reactions with water (H
                    2
                    O)–carbon dioxide fluids. The O isotopic compositions of track-rich hydrated IDPs implicate
                    17,18
                    O-rich ices as the source of H
                    2
                    O involved in their alteration, providing compelling evidence for the presence of a major heavy water reservoir beyond the orbits of the gas giant planets that was largely isolated from inner solar system materials.

title: Phosphatases regulating ERK activation and ERK-dependent cell migration
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
Extracellular signal-regulated kinases (ERKs) have essential roles in development and are implicated in numerous diseases. ERKs are activated by phosphorylation and are regulated by dephosphorylation. To study the ERK phosphatases, we adapted a method to monitor ERK activity in live, unfixed preparations that accommodates the highly dynamic temporal and spatial features of ERK activation. We evaluated 140 human phosphatases using an in vivo reporter (ERK-SPARK) for high-throughput screening in human cells, and we used an in vivo
                    Drosophila
                    model for functional validation of their phosphatase homologs. We found that EYA family phosphatases are critical regulators of ERK signaling both in
                    Drosophila
                    and in mammalian cells and found that inhibition of human EYA4, a homolog of
                    Drosophila
                    Eyes Absent phosphatase, enhances migration of ERK-responsive tumor cells. These findings have important implications for the development of therapeutics.

title: Evolutionarily reinforced GC-rich motif enables non-AUG translation in mammals under eIF1/5MP-mediated fidelity control
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Non-AUG translation contributes to proteome diversity, but its regulatory principles remain unclear. Here, we show that a GCC-rich upstream extension, termed the
                    NAT1
                    motif, acts as a potent enhancer of near-cognate initiation in mammals. Cell-free and reporter assays revealed that eIF1 and 5MP act as conserved inhibitors of non-AUG initiation across mammals and plants, while the
                    NAT1
                    motif enables enhanced initiation within this fidelity framework. Mutational analysis identified −6 and −7 positions within the GCC repeat as key determinants of motif activity. Genome-wide analyses uncovered evolutionary depletion of
                    NAT1
                    -type non-AUG codons in human 5′UTRs, suggesting purifying selection against excessive initiation. Nevertheless, more than a hundred retained sites are associated with genes involved in cell proliferation and migration, suggesting that regulated non-AUG initiation may contribute to disease-relevant translational programs. The motif’s enrichment within GCC repeats further suggests a mechanistic link to repeat-associated non-AUG translation.

title: Basin-scale changes in net primary production from the biogeochemical-Argo array
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Marine net primary production is expected to be affected by climate change. Although remote sensing offers broad spatial and temporal coverage, it is limited to surface observations and cannot capture subsurface variability. Autonomous profiling floats provide critical depth-resolved measurements that help bridge this gap. Here, we use data from the biogeochemical-Argo array to estimate basin-scale change in net primary production using the carbon-based production algorithm. We find statistically significant negative trends across the Atlantic and Southern Oceans and positive trends in the Pacific Ocean. These changes, if occurring in response to climate forcing, raise concern due to the key role of phytoplankton productivity in sustaining marine ecosystems. These trends typically agree in direction and magnitude with those from satellites. Our findings highlight the value of the biogeochemical-Argo array in detecting change in ocean productivity, demonstrating its potential for sustained monitoring. These results underscore the need for integrated observing systems to capture the full extent of changing marine productivity.

title: Does government-assisted relocation help households
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Climate change is intensifying floods and storms, leading governments to consider relocating households away from high-risk areas. Yet, there is little evidence on whether such programs reduce risk or improve household well-being. I evaluate the US Federal Emergency Management Agency’s property acquisition (“buyout”) program using nationwide longitudinal records that track households before and after approval. By comparing households facing similar mapped flood risks, I estimate the program’s effects on relocation, residence in high-risk flood areas, and financial outcomes. Households that participate are more likely to relocate outside Federal Emergency Management Agency–designated flood hazard areas and experience short-term reductions in debt and improvements in neighborhood socioeconomic conditions. However, these benefits are concentrated among participants from wealthier and predominantly white neighborhoods, who relocate more quickly and achieve larger reductions in risk. A benefit-cost analysis shows that the program value depends on implementation costs and realized reductions in flood-risk exposure, with benefit-cost ratios ranging from 0.84 to 1.28 across three scenarios. These results show that government-assisted relocation can be an effective adaptation tool, but its social and economic benefits remain unevenly distributed.
